# Nocta UI

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/README.md

<p align="center">
  <img src="nocta-ui.jpeg" alt="Nocta UI" />
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://nocta-ui.com">Documentation</a> ·
  <a href="https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/issues">Issues</a> ·
  MIT License
</p>

# Nocta UI
Nocta UI is a React component library delivered as source files you control. The CLI keeps installs lightweight and version-free while interactive components build on `@ariakit/react` for accessible behavior out of the box.

## Supported Stacks
- Next.js (App and Pages Router)
- Vite + React
- React Router 7
- TanStack Start
- Custom React workspaces (library or shared UI packages)

## Requirements
- Node.js 18+
- React 18+
- Tailwind CSS v4 present in the workspace
- TypeScript

## Quick Start
**Discover components**
```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli list
```

**Single workspace (Next.js, Vite, and other supported frameworks)**
```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button card badge
```
`init` analyses the current project, writes `nocta.config.json`, updates `nocta.workspace.json`, and drops helpers (`lib/utils.ts`, `lib/icons.ts`) when the workspace owns them. `add` copies registry components into the configured `aliases.components` path and installs any missing dependencies.

**Monorepo linking (shared UI + application)**
```bash
cd packages/ui
npx @nocta-ui/cli init                # choose Shared UI (writes config + helpers)

cd ../apps/web
npx @nocta-ui/cli init                # choose Application, link "ui"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button card     # component source flows into packages/ui
```
- `init` registers both workspaces inside `nocta.workspace.json`. The shared package keeps the helpers and Tailwind tokens; the application records the link.
- `add` runs from the application but writes React source into `packages/ui/src/...`, updates export barrels, and installs dependencies in the owning workspace. Application-side stubs are generated only when required.
- Apps import from the shared package output (`import { Button } from "ui"`). Rebuild the shared package after each add (`bun run --filter ui build` or `bun run --filter ui dev`) so consumers read fresh artefacts.

## `init` Command Reference
- Detects the repo root, framework, package manager, and Tailwind v4.
- Builds a tailored `nocta.config.json` with component and utility aliases.
- Writes shared helpers (`lib/utils.ts`, `components/lib/icons.ts`) when needed.
- Injects Nocta design tokens into your Tailwind entry file for managed workspaces.
- Updates or creates `nocta.workspace.json` so other workspaces can discover this setup.

### Flags
| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Preview every action without touching the filesystem. |
| `--help` | Show command-specific help. |
| `--registry-url` | Point to a custom component registry (or use `NOCTA_REGISTRY_URL`). |

## After `init`
- Add components with `npx @nocta-ui/cli add <component...>`.
- Browse the component registry at `https://nocta-ui.com` or via the CLI prompts.
- Keep your working tree clean; the CLI rolls back if something fails after file writes.

## Contributing
- We welcome contributions! Whether it's bug reports, feature requests, or code contributions, please feel free to open an issue or submit a pull request.
- Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` for detailed guidelines.

## License
- MIT License - see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

# accordion.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/accordion.mdx

title: Accordion
description: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content.

import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";
  DefaultAccordionDemo,
  CardAccordionDemo,
  MultipleAccordionDemo,
  SizeAccordionDemo,

## Installation
Install the Alert component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add accordion
```
Then import the components you need:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  Accordion,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
  AccordionContent
} from '@/components/ui/accordion';

```

## Examples

### Default Accordion

    <DefaultAccordionDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Accordion"
    <Accordion>
      <AccordionItem value="item-1">
        <AccordionTrigger>What is Nocta UI?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Nocta UI is a modern React component library built with performance and accessibility in mind.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="item-2">
        <AccordionTrigger>How to install?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          You can install components using our CLI: <code>npx @nocta-ui/cli add accordion</code>
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="item-3">
        <AccordionTrigger>Does it support dark mode?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Yes! All components in Nocta UI have full dark mode support with automatic switching.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    ```

### Multiple

    <MultipleAccordionDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Multiple Accordion"
    <Accordion type="multiple">
      <AccordionItem value="react">
        <AccordionTrigger>React Basics</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Learn the fundamentals of React - components, props, state and lifecycle.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="typescript">
        <AccordionTrigger>TypeScript Integration</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          How to use TypeScript with React for better type safety.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="testing">
        <AccordionTrigger>Testing Components</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Writing unit and integration tests for React components.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    ```

### Card Variant

    <CardAccordionDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Card Accordion"
    <Accordion variant="card" className="space-y-3">
      <AccordionItem value="account">
        <AccordionTrigger>Account Settings</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Manage your profile, change email address and password.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="security">
        <AccordionTrigger>Security</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Enable two-factor authentication and manage your login sessions.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>

      <AccordionItem value="preferences">
        <AccordionTrigger>Preferences</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Customize the interface theme, language, and notification settings.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    ```

### Sizes

    <SizeAccordionDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Accordion Sizes"
    import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from '@/components/ui/accordion';

    export function SizeAccordionDemo() {
      return (
      <Accordion size="sm">
        <AccordionItem value="small">
          <AccordionTrigger>Small question</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>Short answer in small size.</AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
      <Accordion size="md">
        <AccordionItem value="medium">
          <AccordionTrigger>Standard question</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>Standard answer in default size.</AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
      <Accordion size="lg">
        <AccordionItem value="large">
          <AccordionTrigger>Large question requiring more space</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>
            More detailed answer in larger size, which can contain more content and
            details requiring additional space.
          </AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    ```

## API Reference

### Accordion

    type: {
      description: 'Behavior mode: open one vs many at once',
      type: '"single" | "multiple"',
      default: '"single"',
    variant: {
      description: 'Visual variant',
      type: '"default" | "card"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Size of the accordion',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

### AccordionItem

    value: {
      description: 'Optional id seed for ARIA linking',
    id: {
      description: 'Optional explicit id seed',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Disables the item',
      default: 'false',
    defaultOpen: {
      description: 'Whether the item should be open by default',
      default: 'false',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

### AccordionTrigger

      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

### AccordionContent

      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

# alert.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/alert.mdx

title: Alert
description: A flexible alert component for displaying important messages with multiple variants and dark mode support

  DefaultAlertDemo,
  SimpleAlertDemo,
  AlertVariantsDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"

## Installation
Install the Alert component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add alert
```
Then import the components you need:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  Alert,
  AlertTitle,
  AlertDescription,
} from '@/components/ui/alert';
```

## Examples

### Default Alert

    <DefaultAlertDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Default Alert"
    <Alert>
      <AlertTitle>Information</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        This is a default alert with an information message.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
    ```

### Simple Alert

    <SimpleAlertDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Simple Alert"
    <Alert showIcon="false">
      <AlertDescription>
        A simple alert without title or icon.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
    ```

### Variants

    <AlertVariantsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Alert Variants"
    <Alert variant="default">
      <AlertTitle>Default Alert</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        This is the default variant for general information.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>

    <Alert variant="destructive">
      <AlertTitle>Error</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        Something went wrong. Please try again later.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>

    <Alert variant="warning">
      <AlertTitle>Warning</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        Please review your settings before proceeding.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>

    <Alert variant="success">
      <AlertTitle>Success</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        Your changes have been saved successfully.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
    ```

## Api Reference

      description: 'Alert style variant and icon',
      type: '"default" | "destructive" | "warning" | "success"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Controls padding and spacing',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    showIcon: {
      description: 'Whether to display the variant icon',
      default: 'true',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    children: {
      description: 'Alert content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

### AlertTitle

    as: {
      description: 'HTML element to render',
      type: 'React.ElementType',
      default: '"h5"',
    size: {
      description: 'Controls title typography',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    children: {
      description: 'Title content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

### AlertDescription

    size: {
      description: 'Controls description typography',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    children: {
      description: 'Description content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

# area-chart.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/area-chart.mdx

title: Area Chart
description: Visualise continuous trends and cumulative values with smooth area graphs.

  AreaChart,
  AreaChartBasicDemo,
  AreaChartComparisonDemo,
  AreaChartWithActionsDemo,
  AreaChartWithDataTableDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from '@/components/docs-tab';

Install the Area Chart component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add area-chart
```
Import the component:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  AreaChart,
  AreaChartHeader,
  AreaChartTitle,
  AreaChartDescription,
  AreaChartActions,
  AreaChartGraph,
  AreaChartLegend,
  AreaChartDataTable,
  AreaChartDataTableContent,
} from '@/components/ui/area-chart';
```

## Examples

### Default Area Chart

    <AreaChartBasicDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Monthly Recurring Revenue"
    const revenueTrend = [
      { month: 'Jan', revenue: 25000 },
      { month: 'Feb', revenue: 29325 },
      { month: 'Mar', revenue: 32277 },
      { month: 'Apr', revenue: 32918 },
      { month: 'May', revenue: 31045 },
      { month: 'Jun', revenue: 27253 },
      { month: 'Jul', revenue: 22746 },
      { month: 'Aug', revenue: 18954 },
      { month: 'Sep', revenue: 17081 },
      { month: 'Oct', revenue: 17722 },
      { month: 'Nov', revenue: 20674 },
      { month: 'Dec', revenue: 24999 },
    ];

    <AreaChart data={revenueTrend} xKey="month" yKey="revenue" sortPoints={false}>
      <AreaChartHeader>
        <AreaChartTitle>Monthly Recurring Revenue</AreaChartTitle>
        <AreaChartDescription>
          Track consistent growth across the current fiscal year.
        </AreaChartDescription>
      </AreaChartHeader>
      <AreaChartGraph showYAxisValues={false} height={320} ariaLabel="Monthly recurring revenue trend" />
      <AreaChartLegend />
    </AreaChart>
    ```

### Header with actions

    <AreaChartWithActionsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Session Duration"
    const sessionDuration = [
      { day: 'Mon', minutes: 9.8 },
      { day: 'Tue', minutes: 10.2 },
      { day: 'Wed', minutes: 9.3 },
      { day: 'Thu', minutes: 8.2 },
      { day: 'Fri', minutes: 7.8 },
      { day: 'Sat', minutes: 8.7 },
      { day: 'Sun', minutes: 9.8 },
    ];

    <AreaChart data={sessionDuration} xKey="day" yKey="minutes" seriesLabel="Session duration">
      <AreaChartHeader
        contentClassName="sm:max-w-xs"
        titleClassName="text-lg font-medium"
        actionsClassName="flex-wrap gap-2"
      >
        <AreaChartTitle>Average Session Length</AreaChartTitle>
        <AreaChartDescription>
          Hover to compare behaviour across the week.
        </AreaChartDescription>
        <AreaChartActions>
          <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">
            Export CSV
          </Button>
          <Button size="sm">View Cohort</Button>
        </AreaChartActions>
      </AreaChartHeader>
      <AreaChartGraph
        height={300}
        curve="monotone"
        ariaLabel="Average session duration"
      />
      <AreaChartLegend />
    </AreaChart>
    ```

### Compare multiple series

    <AreaChartComparisonDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Signup Channels"
    const acquisitionChannels = [
      { month: 'Jan', organic: 600, paid: 300 },
      { month: 'Feb', organic: 708, paid: 354 },
      { month: 'Mar', organic: 781, paid: 390 },
      { month: 'Apr', organic: 797, paid: 398 },
      { month: 'May', organic: 751, paid: 375 },
      { month: 'Jun', organic: 656, paid: 328 },
      { month: 'Jul', organic: 543, paid: 271 },
      { month: 'Aug', organic: 448, paid: 224 },
      { month: 'Sep', organic: 402, paid: 201 },
      { month: 'Oct', organic: 418, paid: 209 },
      { month: 'Nov', organic: 491, paid: 245 },
      { month: 'Dec', organic: 600, paid: 300 },
    ];

    <AreaChart
      data={acquisitionChannels}
      xKey="month"
      yKey="organic"
      seriesLabel="Organic signups"
      additionalSeries={[
        { id: 'paid-signups', yKey: 'paid', seriesLabel: 'Paid signups' },
      ]}
    >
      <AreaChartHeader>
        <AreaChartTitle>Signup Channels</AreaChartTitle>
        <AreaChartDescription>
          Track organic and paid conversions side by side.
        </AreaChartDescription>
      </AreaChartHeader>
      <AreaChartGraph ariaLabel="Organic and paid signups over time" />
      <AreaChartLegend />
    </AreaChart>
    ```

### Data table summary

    <AreaChartWithDataTableDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Support Volume"
    const supportTickets = [
      { week: 'Week 1', tickets: 75 },
      { week: 'Week 2', tickets: 84 },
      { week: 'Week 3', tickets: 106 },
      { week: 'Week 4', tickets: 123 },
      { week: 'Week 5', tickets: 123 },
      { week: 'Week 6', tickets: 106 },
      { week: 'Week 7', tickets: 84 },
      { week: 'Week 8', tickets: 75 },
    ];

    <AreaChart data={supportTickets} xKey="week" yKey="tickets" sortPoints={false}>
      <AreaChartHeader>
        <AreaChartTitle>Support Volume</AreaChartTitle>
        <AreaChartDescription>
          Monitor ticket inflow and spot surges that may require staffing changes.
        </AreaChartDescription>
      </AreaChartHeader>
      <AreaChartGraph height={300} ariaLabel="Support tickets created per week" />
      <AreaChartDataTable>
        <AreaChartDataTableContent
          averageLabel="Average tickets"
          averageFormatter={(average) =>
            Math.round(average).toLocaleString(undefined, {
              maximumFractionDigits: 0,
            })
          }
        />
      </AreaChartDataTable>
    </AreaChart>
    ```

## API Reference

### AreaChart

    data: {
      description: 'Primary series consumed by the chart.',
      type: 'TData[]',
      default: '[]',
    xKey: {
      description: 'Property used for the horizontal axis.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
      default: '—',
    yKey: {
      description: 'Property that contains the numeric value for each point.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
      default: '—',
    nameKey: {
      description: 'Optional label key used in tooltips and legends.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
    color: {
      description: 'Override the primary series color.',
      default: 'Design tokens',
    seriesLabel: {
      description: 'Readable label for the primary series.',
      default: 'Derived from nameKey or yKey',
    sortPoints: {
      description: 'Control point ordering or supply a custom comparator.',
      type: 'boolean | ((a: TData, b: TData) => number)',
      default: 'true',
    xFormatter: {
      description: 'Custom formatter for x-axis labels and tooltips.',
      type: '(point: AreaChartPoint<TData>) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.label',
    yFormatter: {
      description: 'Formatter for values shown in tooltips and tables.',
      type: '(point: AreaChartPoint<TData>, meta: { total: number; domain: [number, number] }) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.value.toLocaleString()',
    valueFormatter: {
      description: 'Overrides the numeric formatter when rendering values.',
      type: '(point: AreaChartPoint<TData>, meta: { total: number; domain: [number, number] }) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.value.toLocaleString()',
    additionalSeries: {
      description: 'Render extra series alongside the primary dataset.',
      type: 'AreaChartAdditionalSeries<TData>[]',
      default: '[]',
    children: {
      description: 'Compose headers, graphs, legends, and data tables.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

### AreaChartGraph

    height: {
      description: 'Chart height. Accepts px values or any CSS length.',
      type: 'number | string',
      default: '220px',
    curve: {
      description: 'Spline used to draw the area and line.',
      type:  '"linear" | "monotone" | "natural" | "step"',
      default: '"monotone"',
    showTooltip: {
      description: 'Toggle interactive hover and focus tooltips.',
      default: 'true',
    tooltipRender: {
      description: 'Custom tooltip renderer with access to the computed series.',
      type: '(info: AreaChartTooltipInfo<TData>) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Default tooltip UI',
    showDots: {
      description: 'Render point markers on the line.',
      default: 'true',
    loading: {
      description: 'Display the loading state.',
      default: 'false',
    loadingState: {
      description: 'Replace the default loading placeholder.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset loading state',
    emptyState: {
      description: 'Custom content when there are not enough points.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset empty state',
    error: {
      description: 'Custom error presentation.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset error state',
    ariaLabel: {
      description: 'Accessible label announced by screen readers.',
      default: '"Area chart visualization"',
    showGrid: {
      description: 'Draw horizontal grid lines.',
      default: 'true',
    showXAxisValues: {
      description: 'Render x-axis tick labels.',
      default: 'true',
    showYAxisValues: {
      description: 'Render y-axis tick labels.',
      default: 'true',
    xTickCount: {
      description: 'Target number of ticks on the x-axis.',
      type: 'number',
      default: '4',
    yTickCount: {
      description: 'Target number of ticks on the y-axis.',
      type: 'number',
      default: '5',
    children: {
      description: 'Optional elements layered on top of the SVG.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

### AreaChartHeader

    children: {
      description: 'Header content. Typically `AreaChartTitle`, `AreaChartDescription`, and `AreaChartActions`.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional classes for the header wrapper.',
    contentClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into the primary content column.',
    titleClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into any direct `AreaChartTitle` children.',
    descriptionClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into any direct `AreaChartDescription` children.',
    actionsClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into any direct `AreaChartActions` children.',

### AreaChartTitle

    children: {
      description: 'Title content.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes merged with the default styles.',
    as: {
      description: 'Element or component used to render the title.',
      type: 'React.ElementType',
      default: '"h3"',

### AreaChartDescription

    children: {
      description: 'Supporting copy below the title.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes merged with the default styles.',

### AreaChartActions

    children: {
      description: 'Action elements such as buttons or links.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes merged with the action container.',

### AreaChartLegend

      description: 'Style override applied to the legend wrapper.',

### AreaChartDataTable

    children: {
      description: 'Custom data breakdown that appears below the chart.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes merged with the data table wrapper.',

### AreaChartDataTableContent

      description: 'Additional classes merged with the content wrapper.',
    rowClassName: {
      description: 'Classes applied to each data row, including the summary row.',
    labelClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into the label column.',
    valueClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into the value column.',
    deltaClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into the delta column.',
    showDelta: {
      description: 'Toggle display of the change column.',
      default: 'true',
    deltaFormatter: {
      description: 'Custom formatter for the change column. Receives the current and previous points.',
      type: '(current: AreaChartPoint<TData>, previous: AreaChartPoint<TData> | null) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Percentage change with +/− prefix',
    valueFormatter: {
      description: 'Override how each value cell is rendered.',
      type: '(point: AreaChartPoint<TData>, meta: { total: number; domain: [number, number] }) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Chart value formatter',
    showTotalRow: {
      description: 'Control rendering of the summary row.',
      default: 'true',
    averageLabel: {
      description: 'Label used in the summary row.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: '"Average"',
    averageFormatter: {
      description: 'Format the summary value. Receives the arithmetic mean.',
      type: '(average: number) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'average.toLocaleString()',

# avatar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/avatar.mdx

title: Avatar
description: A versatile avatar component for displaying user profile images, initials, and status indicators with dark mode support

  BasicAvatarDemo,
  AvatarSizesDemo,
  AvatarVariantsDemo,
  StatusDemo,
  FallbackDemo,
  GroupDemo,
  ClickHandlersDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"

## Installation
Install the Avatar component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add avatar
```
Then import the component:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
```

## Examples

### Default Avatar

    <div className="my-6">
      <BasicAvatarDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Avatar"
    <Avatar
      src="https://example.com/avatar.jpg"
      alt="John Doe"
    />

    <Avatar fallback="JD" />

    <Avatar />
    ```

### Sizes

    <div className="my-6">
      <AvatarSizesDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Avatar Sizes"
    <Avatar size="xs" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar size="sm" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar size="md" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar size="lg" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar size="xl" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar size="2xl" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    ```

### Variants

    <div className="my-6">
      <AvatarVariantsDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Avatar Variants"
    <Avatar variant="circle" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar variant="square" src="..." alt="John Doe" />
    <Avatar variant="circle" fallback="JD" />
    <Avatar variant="square" fallback="JD" />
    ```

### Status Indicators

    <div className="my-6">
      <StatusDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Status Indicators"
    <Avatar src="..." alt="John Doe" status="online" />
    <Avatar src="..." alt="Jane Smith" status="away" />
    <Avatar src="..." alt="Mike Johnson" status="busy" />
    <Avatar fallback="AB" status="offline" />
    ```

### Fallback Handling

    <div className="my-6">
      <FallbackDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Fallback Handling"
    <Avatar src="valid-image.jpg" alt="John Doe" />

    <Avatar src="invalid-image.jpg" fallback="JD" alt="John Doe" />

    <Avatar fallback="Sarah Connor" />

    <Avatar fallback="AB" />

    <Avatar />
    ```

### Avatar Groups

    <div className="my-6">
      <GroupDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Avatar Groups"
    <div className="flex items-center">
      <Avatar
        src="avatar1.jpg"
        alt="John Doe"
        className="ring-1 ring-ring-offset"
      />
      <Avatar
        src="avatar2.jpg"
        alt="Jane Smith"
        className="-ml-2 ring-1 ring-ring-offset"
      />
      <Avatar
        src="avatar3.jpg"
        alt="Mike Johnson"
        className="-ml-2 ring-1 ring-ring-offset"
      />
      <Avatar
        fallback="AB"
        className="-ml-2 ring-1 ring-ring-offset"
      />
      <div className="-ml-2 flex h-10 w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-card ring-1 ring-ring-offset text-xs font-medium text-foreground/70">
        +5
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

## API Reference

    src: {
      description: 'The image source URL',
    alt: {
      description: 'Alt text for the image',
      default: '""',
    fallback: {
      description: 'Text to generate initials from, or custom initials',
    size: {
      description: 'The size of the avatar',
      type: '"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl"',
      default: '"md"',
    variant: {
      description: 'The shape variant',
      type: '"circle" | "square"',
      default: '"circle"',
    status: {
      description: 'Status indicator',
      type: '"online" | "offline" | "away" | "busy" | null',
      default: 'null',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes to apply',
      default: '""',

# breadcrumb.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/breadcrumb.mdx

title: Breadcrumb
description: Displays the path to the current resource using a hierarchy of links.

import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";

  BasicBreadcrumbDemo,
  CustomSeparatorDemo,
  ChevronSeparatorDemo,
  EllipsisDemo,
  BreadcrumbSizesDemo,
  GhostVariantDemo,
  ComplexNavigationDemo,

## Installation

    Install the Breadcrumb component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add breadcrumb
    ```
    Then import the components you need:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import {
      Breadcrumb,
      BreadcrumbList,
      BreadcrumbItem,
      BreadcrumbLink,
      BreadcrumbPage,
      BreadcrumbSeparator,
      BreadcrumbEllipsis,
    } from '@/components/ui/breadcrumb';
    ```

## Usage

### Default Breadcrumb

    <BasicBreadcrumbDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Breadcrumb"
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/components">Components</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
    ```

### Custom Separator

    <CustomSeparatorDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Custom Separator"
    <Breadcrumb separator=">">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/docs">Documentation</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Getting Started</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
    ```

### With Icons

    <ComplexNavigationDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="With Icons"
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/" variant="ghost">
            <svg className="w-4 h-4 mr-1" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
              <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={2} d="M3 7v10a2 2 0 002 2h14a2 2 0 002-2V9a2 2 0 00-2-2H5a2 2 0 00-2-2z" />
              <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={2} d="M8 1v6" />
              <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={2} d="M16 1v6" />
            </svg>
            Dashboard
          </BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/users">Users</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Edit Profile</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
    ```

### With Ellipsis

    <EllipsisDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="With Ellipsis"
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>

    ```

### Sizes

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Breadcrumb Sizes"

            <BreadcrumbPage>Small</BreadcrumbPage>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
        </BreadcrumbList>
      </Breadcrumb>

      <Breadcrumb size="md">
        <BreadcrumbList>
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
          </BreadcrumbItem>

          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbPage>Medium</BreadcrumbPage>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
        </BreadcrumbList>
      </Breadcrumb>

      <Breadcrumb size="lg">
        <BreadcrumbList>
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbSeparator />
          <BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbPage>Large</BreadcrumbPage>
          </BreadcrumbItem>
        </BreadcrumbList>
      </Breadcrumb>
    </div>
    ```

### Ghost Variant

    <GhostVariantDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Ghost Variant"

        </BreadcrumbItem>

    ```

## API Reference

### Breadcrumb

    size: {
      description: 'The size of the breadcrumb',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    separator: {
      description: 'Default separator between items',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: '"/"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbList

    size: {
      description: 'Override the size from context',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: 'Inherited',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbItem

    size: {
      description: 'Override the size from context',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: 'Inherited',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbLink

    variant: {
      description: 'The visual style of the link',
      type: '"default" | "ghost"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Override the size from context',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: 'Inherited',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbPage

    size: {
      description: 'Override the size from context',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: 'Inherited',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbSeparator

    size: {
      description: 'Override the size from context',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: 'Inherited',
    children: {
      description: 'Custom separator content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Inherited',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### BreadcrumbEllipsis

      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

# calendar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/calendar.mdx

title: Calendar
description: A fully featured date picker with keyboard navigation, accessibility support, and customizable styling.

import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";

  BasicCalendarDemo,
  CompactCalendarDemo,
  WeekStartsOnMondayDemo,
  WithWeekNumbersDemo,
  DisabledDatesDemo,
  DateRangeDemo,
  CustomFormattingDemo,
  DisabledCalendarDemo,
  EventCalendarDemo

## Installation

    Install the Calendar component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add calendar
    ```
    Then import the component:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/calendar';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Calendar

    <BasicCalendarDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Calendar"
    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar {...calendarValueProps} onChange={setSelectedDate} />
    ```

### Week Configuration

    <WeekStartsOnMondayDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Week Configuration"
    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar
      weekStartsOn={1}
      {...calendarValueProps}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
    ```

### Week Numbers

    <WithWeekNumbersDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Week Numbers"
    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar
      showWeekNumbers
      {...calendarValueProps}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
    ```

### Disabled Dates

    <DisabledDatesDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Disabled Dates"
    // Disable weekends
    const isWeekend = (date: Date) => {
      const day = date.getDay();
      return day === 0 || day === 6;
    };

    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar
      disabledDates={isWeekend}
      {...calendarValueProps}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
    ```

### Date Range Restrictions

    <DateRangeDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Date Range Restrictions"
    const today = new Date();
    const minDate = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate());
    const maxDate = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth() + 2, today.getDate());

    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar
      minDate={minDate}
      maxDate={maxDate}
      {...calendarValueProps}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
    ```

### Custom Formatting

    <CustomFormattingDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Custom Formatting"
    const formatMonth = (date: Date) => {
      const month = date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'long' });
      const year = date.getFullYear();
      return `${month} ${year}`;
    };

    const formatWeekday = (date: Date) => {
      return date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { weekday: 'short' }).toUpperCase();
    };

    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar
      formatMonth={formatMonth}
      formatWeekday={formatWeekday}
      {...calendarValueProps}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
    ```

### Disabled State

    <DisabledCalendarDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Disabled Calendar"
    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date());
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    <Calendar disabled {...calendarValueProps} onChange={setSelectedDate} />
    ```

### Event Handling

    <EventCalendarDemo />
    ```tsx
    const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
    const calendarValueProps = selectedDate ? { value: selectedDate } : {};

    const handleDateSelect = (date: Date | undefined) => {
      setSelectedDate(date);
      if (date) {
        console.log('Selected date:', date.toLocaleDateString());
      }
    };

    <Calendar {...calendarValueProps} onChange={handleDateSelect} />
    {selectedDate && (
      <div className="rounded-lg bg-card p-3">
        <p className="text-sm text-foreground/70">
          Selected: <span className="font-medium">{selectedDate.toLocaleDateString()}</span>
        </p>
      </div>
    )}
    ```

## API Reference

    value: {
      description: 'The selected date (controlled)',
      type: 'Date | undefined',
    defaultValue: {
      description: 'The default selected date (uncontrolled)',
      type: 'Date | undefined',
    onChange: {
      description: 'Callback when date is selected',
      type: '(date: Date | undefined) => void',
    size: {
      description: 'Size of the calendar',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Whether the calendar is disabled',
      default: 'false',
    disabledDates: {
      description: 'Dates to disable',
      type: 'Date[] | ((date: Date) => boolean)',
    minDate: {
      description: 'Minimum selectable date',
      type: 'Date',
    maxDate: {
      description: 'Maximum selectable date',
      type: 'Date',
    showWeekNumbers: {
      description: 'Whether to show week numbers',
      default: 'false',
    showOutsideDays: {
      description: 'Whether to show days from other months',
      default: 'true',
    weekStartsOn: {
      description: 'First day of week (0 = Sunday)',
      type: '0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6',
      default: '0',
    formatMonth: {
      description: 'Custom month formatting function',
      type: '(date: Date) => string',
    formatWeekday: {
      description: 'Custom weekday formatting function',
      type: '(date: Date) => string',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
    'aria-label': {
      description: 'Accessibility label',
      default: '"Calendar"',

# card.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/card.mdx

title: Card
description: A versatile card component system with modular architecture and dark mode support

  SimpleCardDemo,
  CardWithActionsDemo
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"

## Installation

    Install the Card component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add card
    ```
    Then import the components you need:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import {
      Card,
      CardHeader,
      CardTitle,
      CardDescription,
      CardContent,
      CardFooter,
      CardActions,
    } from '@/components/ui/card';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Card

    <SimpleCardDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Simple Card"
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Getting Started</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>
          Learn how to use the Card component in your projects
        </CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p>This is a basic card example showing the fundamental structure.</p>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
    ```

### Card with Actions

    <CardWithActionsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Card with Actions"
    <Card className="max-w-md">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Project Settings</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>
          Manage your project configuration and preferences
        </CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <div className="space-y-3">
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
            <span className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground/70">Status</span>
            <Badge size="sm" variant="success">
              Active
            </Badge>
          </div>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
            <span className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground/70">Members</span>
            <span className="text-sm text-foreground/70">12</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <CardActions>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button variant="default" size="sm">
            Save Changes
          </Button>
        </CardActions>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>

    ```

## API Reference

### Card

    children: {
      description: 'Card content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### CardHeader

    children: {
      description: 'Header content (usually title/description)',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### CardTitle

    children: {
      description: 'Title content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
    as: {
      description: 'Element/component used to render the title',
      type: 'React.ElementType',
      default: '"h3"',

### CardDescription

    children: {
      description: 'Description text',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### CardContent

    children: {
      description: 'Main card content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### CardFooter

    children: {
      description: 'Footer content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

### CardActions

    children: {
      description: 'Action controls (buttons, links, etc.)',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

# chat.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/chat.mdx

title: Chat
description: A comprehensive chat component system with message display, input handling, avatars, timestamps, and real-time messaging capabilities

  BasicChatDemo,
  ChatWithAvatarsDemo,
  ChatWithTimestampsDemo,
  ReadOnlyChatDemo,
  ChatWithActionsDemo,
  CustomStyledChatDemo,
  TypingIndicatorDemo
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"

## Installation

    Install the Chat component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add chat
    ```
    Then import the components you need:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import {
      Chat,
      ChatMessages,
      ChatMessage,
      ChatInput,
      ChatActions,
      TypingIndicator,
      type ChatMessage,
      type TypingUser,
    } from '@/components/ui/chat';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Chat

    <BasicChatDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Chat"
    const [messages, setMessages] = useState<ChatMessage[]>([
      {
        id: '1',
        content: 'Hello! How can I help you today?',
        sender: 'assistant',
        timestamp: new Date(),
        name: 'AI Assistant'
      }
    ]);

    const handleSendMessage = (message: string) => {
      const newMessage: ChatMessage = {
        id: Date.now().toString(),
        content: message,
        sender: 'user',
        timestamp: new Date(),
        name: 'You'
      };

      setMessages(prev => [...prev, newMessage]);
    };

    <Chat
      messages={messages}
      onSendMessage={handleSendMessage}
      placeholder="Type your message here..."
      className="w-full max-w-2xl"
    />
    ```

### Chat with Avatars

    <ChatWithAvatarsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Chat with Avatars"
    const messages: ChatMessage[] = [
      {
        id: '1',
        content: 'Hey everyone! Welcome to the group chat 👋',
        sender: 'assistant',
        timestamp: new Date(),
        name: 'Alice',
        avatar: 'https://example.com/avatar1.jpg'
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        content: 'Thanks for setting this up!',
        sender: 'user',
        timestamp: new Date(),
        name: 'Bob',
        avatar: 'https://example.com/avatar2.jpg'
      }
    ];

    <Chat
      messages={messages}
      onSendMessage={handleSendMessage}
      showAvatars
      placeholder="Join the conversation..."
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
    ```

### Chat with Timestamps

    <ChatWithTimestampsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Chat with Timestamps"
    <Chat
      messages={messages}
      onSendMessage={handleSendMessage}
      showTimestamps
      placeholder="Ask a question..."
      className="w-full max-w-md"
    />
    ```

### Read-Only Chat

    <ReadOnlyChatDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Read-Only Chat"
    <Chat
      messages={messages}
      showTimestamps
      showAvatars
      className="w-full max-w-lg h-80"
      // No onSendMessage prop = read-only mode
    />
    ```

### Typing Indicators

    <TypingIndicatorDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Typing Indicators"
    const [messages, setMessages] = useState<ChatMessage[]>([...]);
    const [typingUsers, setTypingUsers] = useState<TypingUser[]>([]);

    const handleSendMessage = (message: string) => {
      const newMessage: ChatMessage = {
        id: Date.now().toString(),
        content: message,
        sender: 'user',
        timestamp: new Date(),
        name: 'You'
      };

      setMessages(prev => [...prev, newMessage]);

      // Simulate typing indicator
      setTypingUsers([{ id: 'sarah', name: 'Sarah', avatar: 'avatar-url' }]);

      // Remove typing indicator and add response
      setTimeout(() => {
        setTypingUsers([]);
        const response: ChatMessage = {
          id: (Date.now() + 1).toString(),
          content: 'Thanks for your message!',
          sender: 'assistant',
          timestamp: new Date(),
          name: 'Sarah',
          avatar: 'avatar-url'
        };
        setMessages(prev => [...prev, response]);
      }, 2000);
    };

    return (
      <Chat
        messages={messages}
        onSendMessage={handleSendMessage}
        typingUsers={typingUsers}
        showTimestamps
        showAvatars
        placeholder="Send a message to see typing indicators..."
        className="w-full max-w-lg h-96"
      />
    );
    ```

## API Reference

### Message Interface

```tsx lineNumbers title="ChatMessage Interface"
interface ChatMessage {
  id: string;                    // Unique message identifier
  content: string;               // Message text content
  sender: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'; // Message sender type
  timestamp: Date;               // Message timestamp
  avatar?: string;               // Optional avatar URL
  name?: string;                 // Optional sender name
}
```

### TypingUser Interface

```tsx lineNumbers title="TypingUser Interface"
interface TypingUser {
  id: string;                    // Unique user identifier
  name?: string;                 // Optional user name
  avatar?: string;               // Optional avatar URL
}
```

    messages: {
      description: 'Array of chat messages',
      type: 'ChatMessage[]',
      default: '[]',
    onSendMessage: {
      description: 'Callback when message is sent',
      type: '(message: string) => void',
    placeholder: {
      description: 'Input placeholder text',
      default: '"Type a message..."',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Disable chat input',
      default: 'false',
    autoFocus: {
      description: 'Auto-focus input on mount',
      default: 'false',
    maxLength: {
      description: 'Maximum message length',
      type: 'number',
      default: '500',
    showTimestamps: {
      description: 'Show message timestamps',
      default: 'false',
    showAvatars: {
      description: 'Show user avatars',
      default: 'false',
    allowMultiline: {
      description: 'Allow multiline messages',
      default: 'true',
    typingUsers: {
      description: 'Array of users currently typing',
      type: 'TypingUser[]',
      default: '[]',
    variant: {
      description: 'Visual variant',
      type: '"default"',
      default: '"default"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes (used for sizing and custom styling)',
      default: '""',

# checkbox-card.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/checkbox-card.mdx

title: Checkbox Card
description: A selectable card that pairs rich summaries with checkbox behaviour for multi-select interfaces.

  BasicCheckboxCardDemo,
  CheckboxCardGroupDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from '@/components/docs-tab';

## Installation

    Install the Checkbox Card component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add checkbox-card
    ```
    Then import the component where you need it:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import { CheckboxCard } from '@/components/ui/checkbox-card';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Checkbox Card

    <div className="my-6 flex justify-center">
      <BasicCheckboxCardDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Checkbox Card"
    const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState(true);

    <CheckboxCard
      title="Weekly product summary"
      description="Receive a concise recap of the most important product metrics every Monday at 9:00 AM."
      helper="Adjust delivery preferences anytime in notification settings."
      checked={isChecked}
      onCheckedChange={setIsChecked}
    />
    ```

### Integrations Grid

    <CheckboxCardGroupDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Integrations Grid"
    const [selectedIntegrations, setSelectedIntegrations] = useState<string[]>(['slack']);

    const integrations = [
      { id: 'notion', title: 'Notion', description: 'Push tasks and project updates directly into linked workspaces.', meta: 'Beta' },
      { id: 'slack', title: 'Slack', description: 'Send channel notifications whenever critical events happen.', helper: 'Requires workspace admin permissions.' },
      { id: 'figma', title: 'Figma', description: 'Keep your design system components in sync with your product data.' },
      { id: 'github', title: 'GitHub', description: 'Mirror issues, pull requests and code reviews from selected repositories.' }
    ];

    const handleToggle = (id: string) => (next: boolean) => {
      setSelectedIntegrations((prev) => {
        const isSelected = prev.includes(id);
        if (next && !isSelected) return [...prev, id];
        if (!next && isSelected) return prev.filter((item) => item !== id);
        return prev;
      });
    };

    <div className="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
      {integrations.map((integration) => (
        <CheckboxCard
          key={integration.id}
          title={integration.title}
          description={integration.description}
          meta={integration.meta}
          helper={integration.helper}
          checked={selectedIntegrations.includes(integration.id)}
          onCheckedChange={handleToggle(integration.id)}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
    ```

## API Reference

    title: {
      description: 'Primary heading displayed inside the card',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    description: {
      description: 'Supporting text shown under the title',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    meta: {
      description: 'Optional element rendered next to the selection indicator',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    helper: {
      description: 'Helper text displayed at the bottom of the card',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    children: {
      description: 'Extra content rendered between description and helper',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    checked: {
      description: 'Controlled checked state',
      default: 'false',
    defaultChecked: {
      description: 'Initial checked state for uncontrolled usage',
      default: 'false',
    onCheckedChange: {
      description: 'Callback when the selection state changes',
      type: '(checked: boolean) => void',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Disables interaction and visually dims the card',
      default: 'false',
      description: 'Additional classes for the container',
      default: '""',

# Preview the plan without touching disk or dependencies

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/cli-guide/add.mdx

title: Add Components
description: Install one or more Nocta UI components into your configured workspaces.

`add` installs Nocta registry components into the workspaces declared by `nocta.config.json`. It downloads source files, writes them to the right packages, normalises imports, and installs any npm dependencies that are required.

```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button card avatar
# Preview the plan without touching disk or dependencies
npx @nocta-ui/cli add dialog --dry-run
```

## Prerequisites
- A valid `nocta.config.json` in the current directory (run `nocta-ui init` first).
- Tailwind CSS tokens inserted by `init` (optional but recommended).
- Network access to fetch the registry manifest, component source files, and helper assets.

## Command Options
| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Outputs every planned file write and dependency action without touching the filesystem or running package managers. |
| `--help` | Displays usage help. |

Component names are case-insensitive. You can pass multiple names in one run; the CLI resolves internal dependencies automatically.

## How Component Resolution Works
1. Fetch the latest registry manifest and build a lookup table for slugs and display names.
2. For each requested component, load its metadata plus internal dependencies (if component A depends on B, both are installed automatically).
3. Use each file's `target` to decide which workspace should receive it:
   - Files targeting a linked shared UI workspace are written directly into that workspace.
   - Files without an explicit target go to the primary workspace configured in `nocta.config.json`.
4. Component source files are fetched individually from the registry and normalised before writing (import prefixes, alias adjustments etc.).

## File Placement & Import Normalisation
- Files are written relative to the `aliases.components` and `aliases.utils` paths defined in the config.
- Imports that used the registry's default `@/` prefix are rewritten to match your configured alias. React Router projects default to `~/`.
- When a linked workspace exposes a custom import alias (`aliases.components.import`), the CLI emits imports using that alias.
- Existing files trigger a prompt. You can decline to cancel the run, or accept to overwrite. Dry runs list the conflicts but never prompt.

## Export Barrels
- If a workspace defines `exports.components` in `nocta.config.json`, `nocta-ui add` keeps the referenced barrel file in sync.
- New components are appended as named re-exports (`export { Button } from "./components/ui/button";`) inside a marked section so you can still add custom code around it.
- Dry runs preview the statements that would be added without touching disk.
- Shared UI workspaces initialised with the current CLI default to `src/index.ts`, allowing consumers to import from the package root immediately.

## Dependency Management
- Dependencies declared in the registry (for example `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `@ariakit/react`, `@radix-ui/react-icons`) are grouped by workspace.
- The CLI inspects each workspace's `package.json` and installed versions. It only installs packages that are missing or incompatible.
- Install commands are scoped to the right workspace:
  - Workspaces with an npm package name use `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun workspace <name> add`.
  - Otherwise the command runs from the workspace root with `--dir` or `--filter` flags when supported.
- When run with `--dry-run`, the CLI reports which dependencies would be installed or updated without modifying anything.

## Summary Output
At the end of a successful run you will see:
- Files written per workspace, including the component name that produced each file.
- Ready-to-copy import statements using your project's alias prefix.
- Lists of available variants and sizes when the registry provides them.
- Dependency actions (installed, updated, already satisfied) per workspace.

## Monorepo Behaviour
- Linked shared UI workspaces receive the shared component files (and dependency installs) automatically.
- Application workspaces typically only get integration shims or route-specific files; the bulk of the component source lives in the shared package.
- The command honours the same linking rules that `init` recorded in `nocta.config.json` and `nocta.workspace.json`.

## Dry Runs & Automation
- `--dry-run` is ideal for CI or code review. It prints everything that would happen and exits with success without touching files.
- Combine dry runs with `git diff --stat` to preview changes before committing.

## Troubleshooting
- **Component not found** - Run `npx @nocta-ui/cli list` to confirm the canonical component name.
- **Workspace unresolved** - Ensure linked workspaces are defined in `nocta.config.json` and that the relative `config` paths are correct.
- **Dependency conflicts** - Resolve manual overrides in your `package.json` if you want to keep a different version; re-run `add` afterwards to ensure compatibility.

Repeat the command any time you need to scaffold new components or refresh existing ones with the latest registry updates.

---

# Remove cached registry data

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/cli-guide/cache.mdx

title: Manage CLI Cache
description: Inspect and clear the registry and asset cache used by the Nocta CLI.

`cache` reveals where the CLI keeps its on-disk cache and lets you wipe stale registry data. Use it to confirm that environment overrides are picked up or to force the CLI to download fresh manifests before running other commands.

```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli cache
# Remove cached registry data
npx @nocta-ui/cli cache clear --force
```

## What It Does
- Prints the fully resolved cache directory for the current user so you can inspect or script against it.
- Shows whether cached registry metadata and component assets are present before you run network-heavy commands.
- Keeps the filesystem untouched unless you explicitly run `cache clear --force`.

## Cache Contents and Expiration
- The CLI caches registry manifests plus downloaded assets to avoid repeated network calls.
- Default locations follow the platform conventions (`~/.cache/nocta-ui` on Linux, `~/Library/Caches/nocta-ui` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Nocta UI\\Cache` on Windows). Override the directory with `NOCTA_CACHE_DIR`.
- Registry metadata expires after 10 minutes and assets after 24 hours. Override the time-to-live with `NOCTA_CACHE_TTL_MS` and `NOCTA_ASSET_CACHE_TTL_MS` (values in milliseconds).
- If a request fails, the CLI can serve the most recent cached data (up to 30 days old) so you can keep working offline.

## Clearing Cached Data
- Run `npx @nocta-ui/cli cache clear --force` to delete every cached manifest and asset. This is useful when switching to a different registry or when you suspect the cached files are corrupted.
- The `--force` flag prevents accidental deletion; without it the command remains read-only.
- After clearing the cache, the next CLI command will download fresh manifests and assets automatically.

## When to Use It
- Validate that `NOCTA_CACHE_DIR` or TTL overrides are configured correctly.
- Confirm the CLI sees cached files before boarding long flights or working offline.
- Force a refresh after testing against staging or local registry endpoints.

---

# config.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/cli-guide/config.mdx

title: Configuration Files
description: Understand how `nocta.config.json` and `nocta.workspace.json` guide the CLI.

The Nocta CLI maintains two JSON documents: `nocta.config.json` inside each workspace and `nocta.workspace.json` at the repository root. This guide explains their structure and how they are used.

## `nocta.config.json`
Created by `nocta-ui init`, this file describes how the CLI should scaffold components and where shared helpers live.

### Core structure

- `tailwind.css` tells the CLI where to inject design tokens.
- `aliases` control where component files and utilities land and optionally provide a custom import alias.
- `aliasPrefixes` only matter when an alias is a short string; they decide which import prefix (`@`, `~`, etc.) is used.
- `exports.components` (optional) keeps a barrel file up to date when you install components.
- `workspace` stores metadata that lets the CLI coordinate monorepos and link additional workspaces.

### Example: Single workspace inside a repo root

This configuration lives at the repository root and represents a lone application (for example a Next.js project) without separate packages. The CLI writes files relative to the current directory and scopes dependency installs there as well.

```json title="nocta.config.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://nocta-ui.com/registry/schema/config-schema.json",
  "style": "default",
  "tailwind": {
    "css": "app/globals.css"
  },
  "aliases": {
    "components": "components/ui",
    "utils": "lib/utils"
  },
  "aliasPrefixes": {
    "components": "@",
    "utils": "@"
  },
  "workspace": {
    "kind": "app",
    "root": "."
  }
}
```

- No `packageName` is required when the workspace matches the repo root; the CLI simply runs package-manager commands from `.`.
- Omitting `linkedWorkspaces` keeps the configuration focused on this single workspace—add entries later if you split shared UI code into a separate package.

### Example: Application linking a shared UI package

The application workspace keeps its own Tailwind entry point but delegates component installs to a shared UI package. The CLI will sync helpers, exports, and dependencies with the linked workspace.

```json title="apps/web/nocta.config.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://nocta-ui.com/registry/schema/config-schema.json",
  "style": "default",
  "tailwind": {
    "css": "app/globals.css"
  },
  "aliases": {
    "components": "components/ui",
    "utils": "lib/utils"
  },
  "aliasPrefixes": {
    "components": "@",
    "utils": "@"
  },
  "workspace": {
    "kind": "app",
    "packageName": "web",
    "root": "apps/web",
    "linkedWorkspaces": [
      {
        "kind": "ui",
        "packageName": "ui",
        "root": "packages/ui",
        "config": "../../packages/ui/nocta.config.json"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `linkedWorkspaces` let the CLI know which packages should receive component files and dependency updates.
- Paths inside `linkedWorkspaces[].config` are relative to the current workspace, which makes cross-package updates resilient when you move folders.
- Leave `aliasPrefixes` set to `@` unless your project needs a different import character (React Router defaults to `~`).

### Example: Shared UI workspace with export barrel

Shared UI packages usually own component source files, run Tailwind in build pipelines, and expose a barrel file for consumers. The CLI uses this information to decide where to write helpers and when to touch the package manifest.

```json title="packages/ui/nocta.config.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://nocta-ui.com/registry/schema/config-schema.json",
  "style": "default",
  "tailwind": {
    "css": "src/styles.css"
  },
  "aliases": {
    "components": "src/components/ui",
    "utils": "src/lib/utils"
  },
  "aliasPrefixes": {
    "components": "@",
    "utils": "@"
  },
  "exports": {
    "components": {
      "barrel": "src/index.ts",
      "strategy": "named"
    }
  },
  "workspace": {
    "kind": "ui",
    "packageName": "ui",
    "root": "packages/ui"
  }
}
```

- `exports.components` ensures `nocta-ui add` appends new components to the barrel without touching your custom code outside the managed block.
- Shared UI workspaces usually omit `linkedWorkspaces` because other projects link to them; add entries only when you need to push files into sibling libraries.

### Framework Defaults
`init` fills the fields above based on the detected framework:

| Framework | Tailwind CSS file | Component path | Utils path | Alias prefix |
|-----------|------------------|----------------|------------|--------------|
| Next.js (App Router) | `app/globals.css` | `components/ui` | `lib/utils` | `@` |
| Next.js (Pages Router) | `styles/globals.css` | `components/ui` | `lib/utils` | `@` |
| Vite + React | `src/App.css` | `src/components/ui` | `src/lib/utils` | `@` |
| React Router 7 (Framework Mode) | `app/app.css` | `app/components/ui` | `app/lib/utils` | `~` |
| TanStack Start | `src/styles.css` (auto-detected) | `src/components/ui` | `src/lib/utils` | `@` |
| Shared UI / Library | CLI searches common CSS filenames and defaults to `src/styles.css`; component and utility paths live under `src/`. |

You can edit the config after running `init`; future runs merge new information while preserving customisations where possible.

## `nocta.workspace.json`
Stored at the repository root, this manifest tracks every workspace that has run `init`. It enables cross-package coordination when you run commands from different directories.

### Structure
```json
{
  "packageManager": "pnpm",
  "repoRoot": ".",
  "workspaces": [
    {
      "name": "@workspace/ui",
      "kind": "ui",
      "packageName": "@workspace/ui",
      "root": "packages/ui",
      "config": "packages/ui/nocta.config.json"
    },
    {
      "name": "@workspace/admin",
      "kind": "app",
      "packageName": "@workspace/admin",
      "root": "apps/admin",
      "config": "apps/admin/nocta.config.json"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `packageManager` | enum (`"npm"`, `"pnpm"`, `"yarn"`, `"bun"`) | Detected from repo lockfiles. Used for all install commands. |
| `repoRoot` | string (optional) | Normalised path to the repo root (usually `.`). |
| `workspaces` | array | Each entry mirrors information from the corresponding `nocta.config.json`. |

Each workspace entry contains:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Display name (defaults to `root` when no package name is provided). |
| `kind` | enum (`"app"`, `"ui"`, `"library"`) | Workspace role. |
| `packageName` | string (optional) | npm workspace or package name. Helps route package-manager commands. |
| `root` | string | Path from repo root to the workspace. |
| `config` | string | Relative path from repo root to `nocta.config.json`. |

### Lifecycle
- `nocta-ui init` creates or updates the manifest whenever a workspace is registered.
- The file keeps entries sorted by `root` for readability.
- Commands like `add` rely on the manifest to resolve linked workspaces even when you run the CLI from a different directory.

Keep the manifest committed to version control so collaborators share the same workspace topology.

---

# Preview without touching the filesystem

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/cli-guide/init.mdx

title: Init Nocta UI
description: Bootstrap workspaces so they can consume and share Nocta UI components.

`init` bootstraps the current workspace so it can consume Nocta UI components. It analyses your project structure, writes `nocta.config.json`, ensures the repository manifest is updated, and prepares shared helpers. The command respects monorepo layouts and only creates files in the workspace that should own them.

```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
# Preview without touching the filesystem
npx @nocta-ui/cli init --dry-run
```

## Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+ and an existing React project (Next.js, Vite + React, React Router 7, or TanStack Start). Custom apps are supported for shared UI workspaces.
- Tailwind CSS v4 declared (and installed when possible). The command aborts with guidance if v4 is missing.
- Network access to fetch the registry, helper assets, and CSS tokens.
- A clean or at least recoverable working tree -- the CLI performs partial rollback if something fails after writing files.

## Command Options
| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Reports every action (files, dependencies, manifest changes) without touching disk or running package managers. |
| `--help` | Displays command-specific help. |

You can also point the CLI at a custom registry with `--registry-url` or `NOCTA_REGISTRY_URL`.

## Interactive Prompts
`init` inspects your repository and asks extra questions only when needed:
1. **Workspace kind** - If the repo looks like a monorepo and the current folder is not yet registered, choose between Application, Shared UI, or Library. Defaults are inferred from folder names (for example `packages/ui` becomes Shared UI).
2. **Workspace package name** - In monorepos you can provide the npm workspace or package name so other commands can target it precisely. Leave blank to skip.
3. **Linked workspaces** - When configuring an Application workspace inside a monorepo, link one or more existing Shared UI workspaces. Linked workspaces receive shared files and dependency updates when you later run `add`.

## Initialization Flow
1. **Existing config check** - If `nocta.config.json` already exists, the command exits without touching anything.
2. **Repository resolution** - Detects the repo root, loads `nocta.workspace.json` (creating it later if missing), and determines whether multiple workspaces exist.
3. **Framework detection** - Locates the supported framework. For Application workspaces the command aborts with a helpful message when the framework is unknown.
4. **Tailwind verification** - Ensures Tailwind CSS v4 is declared or installed.
5. **Configuration synthesis** - Builds a `nocta.config.json` tailored to the detected framework. The file includes:
   - `tailwind.css` entry where design tokens will be inserted.
   - `aliases.components` and `aliases.utils` pointing at the default component and utility folders.
   - `aliasPrefixes` (usually `@`, `~` for React Router).
   - `workspace` block containing the workspace kind, root, package name, and any links you selected.
6. **Dependency handling** - Reads the registry requirements (React, Tailwind helpers, Ariakit, and more) and only installs them when the current workspace manages its own dependencies. Application workspaces linked to a shared UI package skip these installs because the shared package already owns them.
7. **Helper assets** - When the current workspace manages its own components, the CLI writes:
   - `lib/utils.ts` with the canonical `cn()` helper.
   - `lib/icons.ts` with the base icon map.
   Linked Application workspaces reuse the helpers from the shared UI package and therefore skip these files.
8. **Design tokens** - Adds Nocta semantic color tokens to the configured Tailwind CSS file when the workspace manages its own components. Linked applications skip this step because the shared UI package already owns the tokens.
9. **Workspace manifest** - Creates or updates `nocta.workspace.json` at the repo root so other workspaces can discover this configuration. Package manager detection (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) is stored here as well.
10. **Summary** - Prints a concise report including created files, dependency actions, and linked workspaces. Dry runs label each item as "would do".

## Generated Files
- `nocta.config.json` - Main project configuration (always written unless `--dry-run`).
- `nocta.workspace.json` - Repository manifest (created or updated once per repo).
- `lib/utils.ts` - Shared utility helper (skipped in linked application workspaces).
- `lib/icons.ts` - Base icons module (skipped in linked application workspaces).
- Tailwind CSS entry file - Updated with Nocta design tokens.

All generated paths are made relative to the current workspace. Failures during execution trigger a rollback that deletes any newly created files.

## Re-running the Command
Re-run `init` when you:
- Change framework routing structure (for example, move from Pages Router to App Router).
- Add or rename linked workspaces in a monorepo.
- Want to regenerate the config after manual edits.

Existing files are preserved: helper files are skipped when already present, and design tokens are only inserted once.

## Troubleshooting
- **Tailwind CSS v4 missing** - Install or upgrade Tailwind, then run `init` again.
- **Unsupported framework detected** - Ensure your project matches one of the supported setups or initialise the shared UI package separately before linking from an app.
- **Package manager mismatch** - The CLI honours the lockfile at the repo root; delete stale lockfiles if you intentionally switch managers.

---

# list.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/cli-guide/list.mdx

title: List Components
description: Explore Nocta UI components available in the registry.

`list` queries the Nocta registry and prints an organised catalogue of available components, grouped by category with descriptions, variants, and sizes. Use it to discover component names that can be passed to `nocta-ui add`.

```bash
npx @nocta-ui/cli list
```

## What It Does
- Downloads the registry manifest from the configured endpoint (defaults to `https://nocta-ui.com/registry`).
- Sorts categories alphabetically and prints each component in lowercase (the `add` command is case-insensitive).
- Shows available variants and sizes when the registry provides them.
- Ends with quick examples for installing components.

## Notes
- The command is read-only: it never writes to disk or installs dependencies.
- Override the registry location with `--registry-url` or the `NOCTA_REGISTRY_URL` environment variable.
- Output is designed for humans; use the public registry JSON if you need to script against the data.

---

# design-tokens.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/design-tokens.mdx

title: Design Tokens
description: Reference guide for Nocta UI’s global design tokens — colors, shadows, and radii.
import {TokenTable, colorTokens, shadowTokens, radiusTokens, motionTokens} from "@/components/token-table"

## Colors

All colors are defined in the modern `oklch()` color space, giving precise control over contrast and perceptual brightness across light and dark themes.

<TokenTable category="color" tokens={colorTokens} />

## Shadows

Nocta UI defines a consistent shadow scale for elevation levels.
All shadows use subtle opacity to maintain depth without harsh contrast.

<TokenTable category="shadow" tokens={shadowTokens} />

Shadows are identical in both themes for consistent depth perception.

## Radius

Border radius tokens define how rounded corners appear throughout the system.

<TokenTable category="radius" tokens={radiusTokens} />

Modify this token to globally adjust the curvature of all components in your project.

## Motion

<TokenTable category="motion" tokens={motionTokens} />

Nocta UI hooks this tokens into animations, so updating the curves immediately affects motion primitive.

# dropdown-menu.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/dropdown-menu.mdx

title: Dropdown Menu
description: A dropdown menu component triggered with a standard click, featuring separators, submenus, and disabled states

## Installation

    Install the Dropdown Menu component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"

    ```
    Import the component:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"

    } from '@/components/ui/dropdown-menu';

### Default Dropdown Menu

    const [lastAction, setLastAction] = useState("");

    <DropdownMenu>

        className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant: "secondary", size: "md" }))}
      >
        Open dropdown
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Profile")}>
          <PersonIcon aria-hidden="true" />
          Profile
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Billing")}>
          <CardStackIcon aria-hidden="true" />
          Billing
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Settings")}>
          <GearIcon aria-hidden="true" />
          Settings
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
    ```
