# file-upload.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/file-upload.mdx

title: File Upload
description: Advanced file upload component with drag & drop, progress tracking, validation, and preview support

  FileUploadDemo,
  FileUploadSizesDemo,
  FileUploadImageOnlyDemo,
  FileUploadSingleFileDemo,
  FileUploadDisabledDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"
import { Step, Steps } from "fumadocs-ui/components/steps"

## Installation

    Install the File Upload component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add file-upload
    ```
    Import the component:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import { FileUpload } from '@/components/ui/file-upload';
    ```

## Examples

### Default File Upload

    <FileUploadDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic File Upload"
    const [files, setFiles] = useState<FileUploadFile[]>([]);

    const handleUpload = async (filesToUpload: FileUploadFile[]) => {
      // Your upload logic here
      for (const file of filesToUpload) {
        // Simulate progress
        for (let progress = 0; progress <= 100; progress += 10) {
          await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100));
          setFiles(prevFiles =>
            prevFiles.map(f =>
              f.id === file.id
                ? { ...f, progress, status: progress === 100 ? 'success' : 'uploading' }
                : f
            )
          );
        }
      }
    };

    return (
      <FileUpload
        multiple
        accept="image/*,.pdf,.doc,.docx"
        maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024} // 5MB
        maxFiles={5}
        files={files}
        onFilesChange={setFiles}
        onUpload={handleUpload}
      />
    );
    ```

### Single File Upload

    <FileUploadSingleFileDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Single File Upload"
    <FileUpload
      variant="compact"
      multiple={false}
      accept=".pdf,.doc,.docx"
      maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024} // 10MB
      files={files}
      onFilesChange={setFiles}
      uploadText="Click to upload a document"
      dragText="Drop document here"
    />
    ```

### Image Upload with Preview

    <FileUploadImageOnlyDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Image Upload"
    <FileUpload
      variant="default"
      multiple
      accept="image/*"
      maxSize={2 * 1024 * 1024} // 2MB
      maxFiles={10}
      files={files}
      onFilesChange={setFiles}
      onUpload={handleUpload}
      showPreview={true}
      uploadText="Click to upload images or drag and drop"
      dragText="Drop your images here"
    />
    ```

### Sizes

    <FileUploadSizesDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="File Upload Sizes"
    <FileUpload
      size="sm"
      files={smFiles}
      onFilesChange={setSmFiles}
    />

    <FileUpload
      size="md"
      files={mdFiles}
      onFilesChange={setMdFiles}
    />

    <FileUpload
      size="lg"
      files={lgFiles}
      onFilesChange={setLgFiles}
    />
    ```

### Disabled State

    <FileUploadDisabledDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Disabled State"
    <FileUpload
      disabled
      multiple
      files={files}
      onFilesChange={setFiles}
      uploadText="Upload is disabled"
    />
    ```

## API Reference

    variant: {
      description: 'Visual style variant',
      type: '"default" | "compact"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Size of the upload area',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    multiple: {
      description: 'Allow multiple file selection',
      default: 'false',
    accept: {
      description: 'Accepted file types (MIME types or extensions)',
    maxSize: {
      description: 'Maximum file size in bytes',
      type: 'number',
    maxFiles: {
      description: 'Maximum number of files',
      type: 'number',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Disable the upload component',
      default: 'false',
    files: {
      description: 'Array of files',
      type: 'FileUploadFile[]',
      default: '[]',
    onFilesChange: {
      description: 'Callback when files change',
      type: '(files: FileUploadFile[]) => void',
    onUpload: {
      description: 'Upload function',
      type: '(files: FileUploadFile[]) => Promise<void>',
    showProgress: {
      description: 'Show upload progress',
      default: 'true',
    showPreview: {
      description: 'Show image previews',
      default: 'true',
    uploadText: {
      description: 'Upload zone text',
      default: '"Click to upload or drag and drop"',
    dragText: {
      description: 'Drag over text',
      default: '"Drop files here"',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',

# form.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/form.mdx

title: Form
description: A composable form component with field validation, labels, and actions for building accessible forms

  BasicFormDemo,
  FormWithErrorsDemo,
  ComplexFormDemo,
  FormActionsFormVariantsDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"
import { Step, Steps } from "fumadocs-ui/components/steps"

## Installation

    Install the Form component component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add form
    ```
    Import the component:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import {
      Form,
      FormField,
      FormLabel,
      FormControl,
      FormDescription,
      FormMessage,
      FormActions,
      FormInput,
      FormSubmit,
    } from '@/components/ui/form';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Form

    <BasicFormDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Form"
    <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <FormField name="name">
        <FormLabel required>Full Name</FormLabel>
        <FormControl>
          <Input placeholder="Enter your full name" />
        </FormControl>
        <FormDescription>This will be displayed on your profile.</FormDescription>
      </FormField>

      <FormField name="email">
        <FormLabel required>Email</FormLabel>
        <FormControl>
          <Input type="email" placeholder="Enter your email" />
        </FormControl>
      </FormField>

      <FormActions>
        <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
      </FormActions>
    </Form>
    ```

## Error Handling

Handle validation in two ways:
- Pass an `error` prop to `FormField` and place `<FormMessage />` to display it.
- Or use an Ariakit form store with `validate`/`setError` and place `<FormMessage type="error" />` to read errors from the store.

    <FormWithErrorsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Form with Errors"
    const [errors, setErrors] = useState({
      username: 'Username is already taken',
      password: ''
    });

    <Form>
      <FormField name="username" error={errors.username}>
        <FormLabel required>Username</FormLabel>
        <FormControl>
          <Input placeholder="Choose a username" />
        </FormControl>
        <FormMessage />
      </FormField>

      <FormField name="password" error={errors.password}>
        <FormLabel required>Password</FormLabel>
        <FormControl>
          <Input type="password" placeholder="Create a password" />
        </FormControl>
        <FormDescription>Must be at least 8 characters long.</FormDescription>
        <FormMessage />
      </FormField>
    </Form>
    ```

      description: 'Form submit handler',
      type: '(event: React.FormEvent) => void',
    store: {
      description: 'Optional Ariakit form store',
      type: 'FormStore',
      default: 'useFormStore({})',

### FormField

    children: {
      description: 'Field content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    name: {
      description: 'Field name identifier',
    error: {
      description: 'Error message to display',
    description: {
      description: 'Description text',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

### FormLabel

    children: {
      description: 'Label content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    required: {
      description: 'Show required indicator',
      default: 'false',

### FormMessage

    children: {
      description: 'Message content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    type: {
      description: 'Message type',
      type: '"error" | "success" | "warning"',
      default: '"error"',

### FormActions

    children: {
      description: 'Action buttons',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',
    align: {

      default: '"right"',

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/index.mdx

title: Introduction
description: Nocta UI is a React component library built with a copy-paste philosophy. Instead of shipping as a heavy package, it provides source code you add directly to your project. This gives you full control, easy customization, and no versioning headaches.

## Built on Ariakit

Interactive primitives (menus, dialogs, tabs, roving focus grids, and more) are built on top of <a href="https://ariakit.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">@ariakit/react</a>, ensuring robust accessibility, keyboard navigation, and WAI-ARIA compliance out of the box.

## Getting Started

Install the CLI and add components to your project:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button card badge
```

---

# line-chart.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/line-chart.mdx

title: Line Chart
description: Track evolving metrics and dynamic changes using clear, continuous line plots.

  LineChart,
  LineChartBasicDemo,

  LineChartWithActionsDemo,

import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from '@/components/docs-tab';

Install the Line Chart component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add line-chart
```
Import the component:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  LineChart,
  LineChartHeader,
  LineChartTitle,
  LineChartDescription,
  LineChartActions,
  LineChartGraph,
  LineChartLegend,
  LineChartDataTable,
  LineChartDataTableContent,
} from '@/components/ui/line-chart';
```

## Examples

### Default Line Chart

    <LineChartBasicDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Monthly Recurring Revenue"
    const revenueTrend = [
      { month: "Jan", revenue: 18500 },
      { month: "Feb", revenue: 32400 },
      { month: "Mar", revenue: 27950 },
      { month: "Apr", revenue: 46820 },
      { month: "May", revenue: 39210 },
      { month: "Jun", revenue: 58740 },
      { month: "Jul", revenue: 31180 },
      { month: "Aug", revenue: 74220 },
      { month: "Sep", revenue: 42110 },
      { month: "Oct", revenue: 91280 },
      { month: "Nov", revenue: 50640 },
      { month: "Dec", revenue: 84310 },
    ];

    <LineChart data={revenueTrend} xKey="month" yKey="revenue" sortPoints={false}>
      <LineChartHeader>
        <LineChartTitle>Streaming Revenue by Month</LineChartTitle>
        <LineChartDescription>
          See how launches, campaigns, and seasonality impact your monthly earnings.
        </LineChartDescription>
      </LineChartHeader>
      <LineChartGraph showYAxisValues={false} height={320} ariaLabel="Monthly streaming revenue pattern" />
      <LineChartLegend />
    </LineChart>
    ```

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Support Volume"

      <LineChartGraph showGrid ariaLabel="Support tickets created per week" />

        <LineChartDataTableContent

              maximumFractionDigits: 0,
            })
          }
        />
      </LineChartDataTable>
    </LineChart>
    ```

## API Reference

### LineChart

    data: {
      description: 'Primary series consumed by the chart.',
      type: 'TData[]',
      default: '[]',
    xKey: {
      description: 'Property used for the horizontal axis.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
      default: '—',
    yKey: {
      description: 'Property that contains the numeric value for each point.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
      default: '—',
    nameKey: {
      description: 'Optional label key used in tooltips and legends.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
    color: {
      description: 'Override the primary series color.',
      default: 'Design tokens',
    seriesLabel: {
      description: 'Readable label for the primary series.',
      default: 'Derived from nameKey or yKey',
    sortPoints: {
      description: 'Control point ordering or supply a custom comparator.',
      type: 'boolean | ((a: TData, b: TData) => number)',
      default: 'true',
    xFormatter: {
      description: 'Custom formatter for x-axis labels and tooltips.',
      type: '(point: LineChartPoint<TData>) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.label',
    yFormatter: {
      description: 'Formatter for values shown in tooltips and tables.',
      type: '(point: LineChartPoint<TData>, meta: { total: number; domain: [number, number] }) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.value.toLocaleString()',
    valueFormatter: {
      description: 'Overrides the numeric formatter when rendering values.',
      type: '(point: LineChartPoint<TData>, meta: { total: number; domain: [number, number] }) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'point.value.toLocaleString()',
    additionalSeries: {
      description: 'Render extra series alongside the primary dataset.',
      type: 'LineChartAdditionalSeries<TData>[]',
      default: '[]',
    children: {
      description: 'Compose headers, graphs, legends, and data tables.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

    height: {

    loading: {

# menubar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/menubar.mdx

title: Menubar
description: A top-level application menubar with grouped actions, submenus, and full keyboard navigation

  BasicMenubarDemo,
  MenubarDisabledDemo,
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";
import { Step, Steps } from "fumadocs-ui/components/steps";

## Installation

    Install the Menubar component with the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add menubar
    ```
    Import only the pieces you need:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import {
      Menubar,
      MenubarMenu,
      MenubarTrigger,
      MenubarContent,
    } from '@/components/ui/menubar';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Menubar

    <BasicMenubarDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Menubar"
    const [lastAction, setLastAction] = useState('No action selected');

    <Menubar>
      <MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
        <MenubarContent>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("New project")}>
            <FilePlusIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            New project
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Open file")}>
            <OpenInNewWindowIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Open file
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Save")}>
            <EnterIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Save
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarSeparator />
          <MenubarSub>
            <MenubarSubTrigger>
              <Share1Icon aria-hidden="true" />
              Share
            </MenubarSubTrigger>
            <MenubarSubContent>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Share to email")}>
                Email
              </MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Share to teams")}>
                Teams
              </MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Copy link")}>
                Copy link
              </MenubarItem>
            </MenubarSubContent>
          </MenubarSub>
          <MenubarSeparator />
          <MenubarItem destructive onClick={() => setLastAction("Close window")}>
            Close window
          </MenubarItem>
        </MenubarContent>
      </MenubarMenu>

      <MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarTrigger>Edit</MenubarTrigger>
        <MenubarContent>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Undo")}>
            <ReloadIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Undo
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Redo")}>
            <ReloadIcon aria-hidden="true" className="rotate-180" />
            Redo
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarSeparator />
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Cut")}>
            <ScissorsIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Cut
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Copy")}>
            <CopyIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Copy
          </MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => setLastAction("Paste")}>
            <DotsHorizontalIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            Paste
          </MenubarItem>
        </MenubarContent>
      </MenubarMenu>
    </Menubar>
    ```

### Disabled States

    <MenubarDisabledDemo />

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Disabled Menubar Items"
      </MenubarMenu>
    </Menubar>
    ```

## API Reference

### Menubar

    children: {
      description: 'Menubar menus',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

# monorepo.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/monorepo.mdx

title: Monorepo Setup
description: Link a shared Nocta UI workspace to an application using Bun workspaces.

Nocta UI treats shared UI workspaces as the source of truth for component files. In a monorepo you can run CLI commands from an application workspace while the actual React source lives inside a sibling package. This guide recreates the Bun + Next.js example step by step so you can adapt it to your own tooling.

## Prerequisites
- Bun 1.1 or newer
- Node.js (for occasional `npx` utilities)
- Git (recommended for tracking generated files)

## Repository Layout

```
nocta-bun-monorepo
├── apps/
│   └── web     (Next.js application)
└── packages/
    └── ui      (shared Nocta UI workspace)
```

## Step-by-step

    ### 1. Initialise the repo root

   ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    mkdir nocta-bun-monorepo
    cd nocta-bun-monorepo
    bun init --yes
    ```

    Update `package.json` so Bun knows where workspaces live:

    ```json lineNumbers title="package.json"
    {
      "name": "nocta-bun-monorepo",
      "module": "index.ts",
      "type": "module",
      "private": true,
      "workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"],  // [!code highlight]
      "devDependencies": {
        "@types/bun": "latest"
      },
      "peerDependencies": {
        "typescript": "^5"
      }
    }
    ```
    ### 2. Scaffold the shared UI workspace (`packages/ui`)

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    mkdir -p packages/ui
    cd packages/ui
    bun init --yes
    bun add -D tsc-alias rimraf concurrently tailwindcss
    ```

    Configure TypeScript with alias support so registry files that import from `@/...` compile cleanly:

    ```json lineNumbers title="tsconfig.json"
    {
      "compilerOptions": {
        "lib": ["ESNext","DOM"],
        "target": "ESNext",
        "module": "Preserve",
        "moduleDetection": "force",
        "jsx": "react-jsx",
        "allowJs": true,
        "moduleResolution": "bundler",
        "allowImportingTsExtensions": false,   // [!code highlight]
        "verbatimModuleSyntax": false,  // [!code highlight]
        "outDir": "dist",   // [!code highlight]
        "declaration": true,   // [!code highlight]
        "declarationDir": "dist",   // [!code highlight]
        "baseUrl": ".",   // [!code highlight]
        "paths": {   // [!code highlight]
          "@/*": ["./src/*"]   // [!code highlight]
        },   // [!code highlight]
        "strict": true,
        "skipLibCheck": true,
        "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
        "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
        "noImplicitOverride": true,
        "noUnusedLocals": false,
        "noUnusedParameters": false,
        "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": false
      }
    }
    ```

    Add build scripts so the package emits compiled artefacts to `dist/`:

    ```json lineNumbers title="package.json"
    {
      "name": "ui",
      "type": "module",
      "private": true,
      "files": ["dist"],   // [!code highlight]
      "exports": {   // [!code highlight]
        ".": {   // [!code highlight]
          "import": "./dist/src/index.js",   // [!code highlight]
          "types": "./dist/src/index.d.ts"   // [!code highlight]
        },   // [!code highlight]
        "./dist/styles.css": "./dist/styles.css"   // [!code highlight]
      },   // [!code highlight]
      "main": "./dist/src/index.js",   // [!code highlight]
      "module": "./dist/src/index.js",   // [!code highlight]
      "types": "./dist/src/index.d.ts",   // [!code highlight]
      "peerDependencies": {
        "typescript": "^5.9.3"
      },
      "devDependencies": {
        "@types/bun": "latest",
        "concurrently": "^9.2.1",
        "rimraf": "^6.0.1",
        "tailwindcss": "^4.1.15",
        "tsc-alias": "^1.8.16",
        "typescript": "^5.9.3"
      },
      "scripts": {   // [!code highlight]
        "build": "bun run clean && bun run build:css && bun run build:ts",   // [!code highlight]
        "build:css": "mkdir -p dist && bunx tailwindcss --input src/styles.css --output dist/styles.css --minify",   // [!code highlight]
        "build:ts": "tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc-alias -p tsconfig.json",   // [!code highlight]
        "clean": "rimraf dist",   // [!code highlight]
        "dev": "concurrently -k -n TS,ALIAS,CSS \"bun run dev:ts\" \"bun run dev:alias\" \"bun run dev:css\"",   // [!code highlight]
        "dev:ts": "tsc -w -p tsconfig.json",   // [!code highlight]
        "dev:alias": "tsc-alias -w -p tsconfig.json",   // [!code highlight]
        "dev:css": "bunx tailwindcss --input src/styles.css --output dist/styles.css --watch"   // [!code highlight]
      }   // [!code highlight]
    }
    ```

    `tsc-alias` rewrites the `@/...` imports in the compiled output so downstream apps can resolve files without custom TS paths.
    ### 3. Set up the Next.js app (`apps/web`)

   ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    cd ../../
    mkdir -p apps/web
    cd apps/web
    bun create next-app@latest . --yes
    ```

    Point the app at the shared workspace via Bun workspaces:

    ```json lineNumbers title="package.json"
    {
      "name": "web",
      "version": "0.1.0",
      "private": true,
      "scripts": {
        "dev": "next dev",
        "build": "next build",
        "start": "next start",
        "lint": "eslint"
      },
      "dependencies": {
        "next": "16.0.0",
        "react": "19.2.0",
        "react-dom": "19.2.0",
        "ui": "workspace:*"   // [!code highlight]
      },
      "devDependencies": {
        "@tailwindcss/postcss": "^4",
        "@types/node": "^20",
        "@types/react": "^19",
        "@types/react-dom": "^19",
        "eslint": "^9",
        "eslint-config-next": "16.0.0",
        "tailwindcss": "^4",
        "typescript": "^5"
      }
    }
    ```

    Import the compiled UI stylesheet once inside `app/layout.tsx` (or your preferred root file):

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="app/layout.tsx"
    import "ui/dist/styles.css";
    ```
    ### 4. Initialise the Nocta CLI

    Run `init` inside each workspace so the CLI records relationships and writes helpers.

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    cd packages/ui
    npx @nocta-ui/cli init                # choose Shared UI

    cd ../../apps/web
    npx @nocta-ui/cli init                # choose Application and link "ui"
    ```

    - The shared UI workspace receives `nocta.config.json`, helper utilities, Tailwind tokens, and an entry inside `nocta.workspace.json`.
    - The application workspace stores a link to `ui`, so future `nocta-ui add` runs from `apps/web` copy React source into `packages/ui`.
    ### 5. Install components and rebuild the shared package

    From `apps/web` install components like normal:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add button card
    ```

    The CLI writes component source files into `packages/ui/src/...`, updates export barrels, and scopes dependency installs to the owning workspace. Rebuild or watch the shared package after each run so the compiled artefacts remain fresh:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    bun run --filter ui build
    # or keep everything hot
    bun run --filter ui dev
    ```

## Using the Components

After rebuilding, import components from the shared package inside your application:

```tsx lineNumbers title="apps/web/app/page.tsx"
import { Button } from "ui";

export default function Page() {
  return <Button>Ready for launch</Button>;
}
```

You now have a monorepo-aware workflow where shared UI code lives in `packages/ui`, applications call CLI commands from their own directory, and Bun handles dependencies for the entire workspace.

---

# nextjs.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/nextjs.mdx

title: Next.js Installation
description: Step-by-step guide to install and configure Nocta UI with Next.js

## Create Next.js Project

First, create a new Next.js project:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx create-next-app@latest my-app
  --typescript
  --eslint
  --tailwind
  --app
  --turbopack
  --import-alias "@/*"
cd my-app
```

## Install Nocta UI

Initialize Nocta UI in your project. This will automatically install all required dependencies:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
```

## Add Components

Now you can add specific components that you need:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button
npx @nocta-ui/cli add card
npx @nocta-ui/cli add badge
```

## Usage

Now you can import and use Nocta UI components in your Next.js application:

```tsx lineNumbers title="src/app/page.tsx"
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <div className="p-8">
      <Card className="max-w-md">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Welcome to Nocta UI</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <div className="space-y-4">
            <Button variant="default">
              Get Started
            </Button>
            <Badge variant="secondary">
              Next.js Ready
            </Badge>
          </div>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

You're all set! Use the Nocta UI CLI to pull components straight into your Next.js application whenever you need them.

---

# otp-input.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/otp-input.mdx

title: OTP Input
description: Secure multi-digit input for one-time passwords with paste support, validation states, and full keyboard control.

import { OTPInputDemo } from '@/demos';
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"
import { Step, Steps } from "fumadocs-ui/components/steps"

## Installation

    Install the OTP Input component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add otp-input
    ```
    Import the component:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import { OTPInput } from '@/components/ui/otp-input';
    ```

## Examples

### Default OTP Input

    <OTPInputDemo />
```tsx lineNumbers title="OTP verification flow"
const [code, setCode] = useState('');
const [status, setStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'success' | 'error'>('idle');

const helperText =
  status === 'idle' ? 'Enter the 6-digit code sent to your phone.' : undefined;
const successMessage =
  status === 'success' ? 'Code captured successfully.' : undefined;

return (
  <OTPInput
    length={6}
    value={code}
    onChange={(nextValue) => {
      setCode(nextValue);
      if (nextValue.length === 6) {
        setStatus('success');
      } else if (status !== 'idle') {
        setStatus('idle');
      }
    }}
    variant={status === 'error' ? 'error' : status === 'success' ? 'success' : 'default'}
    label="One-time password"
    helperText={helperText}
    successMessage={successMessage}
    autoComplete="one-time-code"
  />
);
```

## API Reference

    onChange: {

    onComplete: {
      description: 'Fires when all cells are filled.',
      type: '(value: string) => void',
    variant: {
      description: 'Visual style used for the cells.',
      type: '"default" | "success" | "error"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Controls the cell size and spacing.',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    label: {
      description: 'Optional label rendered above the field.',
    helperText: {
      description: 'Helper text displayed below the field.',
    disabled: {
      description: 'Disables all cells when true.',
      default: 'false',
    readOnly: {
      description: 'Prevents editing while keeping the inputs focusable.',
      default: 'false',
    autoFocus: {
      description: 'Automatically focuses the first cell on mount.',
      default: 'false',
    errorMessage: {
      description: 'Error text shown when `variant="error"`.',
    successMessage: {
      description: 'Success text shown when `variant="success"`.',
    containerClassName: {
      description: 'Class name applied to the outer wrapper.',

    cellClassName: {
      description: 'Class name applied to each OTP cell.',

      description:
        'When provided, the component renders a hidden input so values submit with forms.',

# pie-chart.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/pie-chart.mdx

title: Pie Chart
description: Compare parts-to-whole relationships with classic and donut layouts.

### Donut with labels

    <PieChartDonutDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Donut Chart"
    const planData = [
	{ plan: 'Starter', users: 1280 },
	{ plan: 'Growth', users: 2870 },
	{ plan: 'Scale', users: 1960 },
	{ plan: 'Enterprise', users: 620 },
    ];

    <PieChart data={planData} valueKey="users" nameKey="plan">
      <PieChartHeader>

        <PieChartDescription>
          Donut layout highlights relative share of subscriptions.
        </PieChartDescription>
      </PieChartHeader>
      <PieChartGraph
        height={320}
        innerRadius="55%"
        padAngle={2}
        cornerRadius={4}
        ariaLabel="Active accounts by plan"
      >
        <div className="text-center">
          <p className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-foreground/50">
            Total users
          </p>
          <p className="text-2xl font-medium text-foreground">
            {data.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.users, 0).toLocaleString()}
          </p>
        </div>
      </PieChartGraph>
      <PieChartLegend />
    </PieChart>
    ```

### Header with actions

    <PieChartWithActionsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Campaign Conversions"
    // Requires Button from '/ui/button'
    const campaignData = [
      { campaign: 'Email', conversions: 420 },
      { campaign: 'Paid Ads', conversions: 310 },
      { campaign: 'Webinar', conversions: 180 },
      { campaign: 'Social', conversions: 260 },
    ];

    <PieChart data={campaignData} valueKey="conversions" nameKey="campaign">
      <PieChartHeader
        contentClassName="sm:max-w-xs"
        actionsClassName="flex-wrap gap-2"
      >
        <PieChartTitle>Campaign Conversions</PieChartTitle>
        <PieChartDescription>
          Compare how each acquisition channel performed this quarter.
        </PieChartDescription>
        <PieChartActions>
          <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">
            Download CSV
          </Button>
          <Button size="sm">View Report</Button>
        </PieChartActions>
      </PieChartHeader>
      <PieChartGraph
        height={300}
        innerRadius="45%"
        padAngle={1}
        ariaLabel="Campaign conversion share"
      />
      <PieChartLegend />
    </PieChart>
    ```

### Data table summary

    <PieChartWithDataTableDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Revenue Breakdown"
    const revenueData = [
      { region: 'North America', revenue: 48800 },
      { region: 'Europe', revenue: 31200 },
      { region: 'Asia Pacific', revenue: 27600 },
      { region: 'Latin America', revenue: 16450 },
    ];
    <PieChart
      data={revenueData}
      valueKey="revenue"
      nameKey="region"
      sortSlices
    >
      <PieChartHeader>
        <PieChartTitle>Quarterly Revenue by Region</PieChartTitle>
        <PieChartDescription>
          Break down revenue contribution and view the detailed table below.
        </PieChartDescription>
      </PieChartHeader>
      <PieChartGraph height={300} ariaLabel="Revenue share by region" />
        <PieChartDataTableContent
          totalLabel="Total revenue"
          totalFormatter={(total) =>
            total.toLocaleString(undefined, {
              style: 'currency',
              currency: 'USD',
              maximumFractionDigits: 0,
            })
          }
        />
      </PieChartDataTable>
    </PieChart>
    ```

## API Reference

### PieChart

    data: {
      description: 'Data slices consumed by the chart.',
      type: 'TData[]',
      default: '[]',
    valueKey: {
      description: 'Property that contains the numeric value for each slice.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
      default: '—',
    nameKey: {
      description: 'Optional property used for labels in tooltips and legends.',
      type: 'Extract<keyof TData, string>',
    colors: {
      description: 'Palette applied to slices, defaults to the theme chart tokens.',
      type: 'readonly string[]',
      default: 'Design tokens',
    sortSlices: {
      description: 'Enable automatic sorting or provide your own comparator.',
      type: 'boolean | ((a: TData, b: TData) => number)',
      default: 'false',
    valueFormatter: {
      description: 'Customise values shown in tooltips and legends.',
      type: '(slice, meta) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'value.toLocaleString()',
    labelFormatter: {
      description: 'Override the label text for each slice.',
      type: '(slice) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'nameKey or generated label',
    children: {
      description: 'Compose headers, charts, legends, and data tables.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

### PieChartGraph

    height: {
      description: 'Chart height. Accepts px values or any CSS length.',
      type: 'number | string',
      default: '280',
    innerRadius: {
      description: 'Convert the pie into a donut by setting the inner radius (px or % of outer radius).',
      type: 'number | string',
      default: '0',
    outerRadius: {
      description: 'Override the outer radius (px or %, useful for tight layouts).',
      type: 'number | string',
      default: 'auto',
    padAngle: {
      description: 'Gap between slices in degrees.',
      type: 'number',
      default: '0',
    cornerRadius: {
      description: 'Rounded corners for slices.',
      type: 'number',
      default: '0',
    startAngle: {
      description: 'Start angle in degrees (0 = right side).',
      type: 'number',
      default: '0',
    endAngle: {
      description: 'End angle in degrees.',
      type: 'number',
      default: '360',
    showTooltip: {
      description: 'Enable hover and focus tooltips.',
      default: 'true',
    tooltipRender: {
      description: 'Custom tooltip renderer. Receives slice data, value, and percentage.',
      type: '(info: PieChartTooltipInfo<TData>) => React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Default tooltip UI',
    loading: {
      description: 'Display the loading state.',
      default: 'false',
    loadingState: {
      description: 'Content displayed while `loading` is true.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset placeholder',
    emptyState: {
      description: 'Custom content when no slices are available.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset placeholder',
    error: {
      description: 'Error state content.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      default: 'Preset message',
    ariaLabel: {
      description: 'Accessible label applied to the chart SVG.',
      default: 'undefined (falls back to "Pie chart visualization")',
    children: {
      description: 'Content rendered centered over the chart area.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes for the outer wrapper.',
    style: {
      description: 'Inline styles applied to the outer wrapper.',
      type: 'React.CSSProperties',

### PieChartHeader

    children: {
      description: 'Header content. Typically `PieChartTitle`, `PieChartDescription`, and `PieChartActions`.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
      description: 'Additional classes for the header wrapper.',
    contentClassName: {
      description: 'Classes merged into the primary content column (title + description).',


    <ProgressVariantsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Progress Variants"

    ```

### Animated Progress

    <AnimatedDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Animated Progress"
    const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);

    useEffect(() => {
      const timer = setInterval(() => {
        setProgress((prev) => prev >= 100 ? 0 : prev + 10);
      }, 500);
      return () => clearInterval(timer);
    }, []);

    return <Progress value={progress} variant="success" showLabel />
    ```

### Without Label

    <WithoutLabelDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Progress Without Label"
    <Progress value={40} />
    <Progress value={70} variant="success" />
    <Progress value={85} variant="warning" />
    ```

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Radio Group with Descriptions"
        label="Starter"
        description="Basic plan for personal projects"
      />
      <RadioGroupItem
        value="pro"
        label="Pro"
        description="Advanced features for growing teams"
      />
      <RadioGroupItem
        value="enterprise"
        label="Enterprise"

      />
    </RadioGroup>
    ```

    <div className="my-6">
      <HorizontalRadioGroupDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Horizontal Radio Group"
    const [alignment, setAlignment] = useState('center');

    <RadioGroup
      value={alignment}
      onValueChange={(v) => setAlignment(v as string)}
      className="flex flex-row gap-4"
      aria-label="Alignment"
    >
      <RadioGroupItem value="start" label="Start" />
      <RadioGroupItem value="center" label="Center" />
      <RadioGroupItem value="end" label="End" />
    </RadioGroup>
    ```

# reactrouter.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/reactrouter.mdx

title: React Router Installation
description: Step-by-step guide to install and configure Nocta UI with React Router 7

## Create React Router Project

First, create a new React Router project:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx create-react-router@latest my-app
cd my-app
```

## Install Nocta UI

Initialize Nocta UI in your project. This will automatically install all required dependencies:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
```

## Add Components

Now you can add specific components that you need:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button
npx @nocta-ui/cli add card
npx @nocta-ui/cli add badge
```

## Usage

Now you can import and use Nocta UI components in your React Router application:

```tsx lineNumbers title="app/routes/home.tsx"
import { Button } from '~/components/ui/button';
import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent, CardTitle } from '~/components/ui/card';
import { Badge } from '~/components/ui/badge';

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <div className="p-8">
      <Card className="max-w-md">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Welcome to Nocta UI</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <div className="space-y-4">
            <Button variant="default">
              Get Started
            </Button>
            <Badge variant="secondary">
              React Router Ready
            </Badge>
          </div>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

You're all set! Use the Nocta UI CLI to pull components straight into your React Router application whenever you need them.

---

# scroll-area.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/scroll-area.mdx

description: A stylized scroll container with composable viewport, custom indicators, and hover or scroll-driven visibility

import { ScrollAreaBasicDemo, ScrollAreaHorizontalDemo } from '@/demos';

## Installation

Install the Scroll Area component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add scroll-area
```
Import the pieces you need:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import { ScrollArea } from '@/components/ui/scroll-area';
```

## Examples

### Default Scroll Area

    <ScrollAreaBasicDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Scrollable Panel"
    const notifications = [
      { title: 'Product launch', time: '2m ago', body: 'Release goes live tomorrow at 9:00 AM.' },
      { title: 'New mention', time: '18m ago', body: 'Marta mentioned you in #design-system.' },
      // ...
    ];

    <ScrollArea className="h-64 w-full max-w-md">
      <div className="space-y-4">
        {notifications.map((notification) => (
          <div
            key={notification.title}
            className="relative rounded-lg border border-border/60 bg-card-muted/40 p-4 shadow-xs card-highlight"
          >
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between text-sm font-medium text-foreground">
              <span>{notification.title}</span>
              <span className="text-foreground/60">{notification.time}</span>
            </div>
            <p className="mt-2 text-sm leading-relaxed text-foreground/70">
              {notification.body}
            </p>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ScrollArea>
    ```

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Horizontal Scroll"
    const frameworks = ['Next.js', 'Expo', 'Remix', 'SvelteKit'];

    <ScrollArea type="scroll" direction="horizontal" className="w-full max-w-3xl">
      <div className="flex w-max gap-3 whitespace-nowrap text-sm font-medium p-3">
        {frameworks.map((framework) => (
          <span
            key={framework}
            className="relative rounded-full border border-border/60 bg-card px-4 py-2 shadow-xs card-highlight"
          >
            {framework}
          </span>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ScrollArea>
    ```

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Default Select"
        <SelectItem value="grape">Grape</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="pineapple">Pineapple</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
    ```

title: Separator

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Card Divider"
    </div>

    ```

      description: 'Controls the thickness of the line',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"sm"',

# sidebar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/sidebar.mdx

title: Sidebar
description: A collapsible application sidebar with floating controls, peek interactions, and a dedicated content inset.

import { SidebarWorkspaceDemo } from '@/demos';
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from '@/components/docs-tab';

## Installation

    Install the Sidebar package using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add sidebar
```
    Then import the primitives you need:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  Sidebar,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarFooter,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupAction,
  SidebarGroupContent,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarInput,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarMenuSub,
  SidebarMenuSubButton,
  SidebarMenuSubItem,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarSeparator,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/sidebar";
```

## Examples

### Default Sidebar

    <SidebarWorkspaceDemo />
```tsx lineNumbers title="Sidebar layout"
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { Button } from "../button";
import * as RadixIcons from "@radix-ui/react-icons";
import type { CommandKItem } from "../command-k";
import {
  Sidebar,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarFooter,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupAction,
  SidebarGroupContent,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarInput,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarMenuSub,
  SidebarMenuSubButton,
  SidebarMenuSubItem,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarSeparator,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "./sidebar";

type WorkspaceNavChild = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  icon: keyof typeof RadixIcons;
  tooltip?: string;
};

type WorkspaceNavItem = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  icon: keyof typeof RadixIcons;
  tooltip?: string;
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  children?: WorkspaceNavChild[];
};

const workspaceNavigation: WorkspaceNavItem[] = [
  {
    id: "introduction",
    title: "Introduction",
    icon: "HomeIcon",
    tooltip: "Start with an overview of the system",
  },
  {
    id: "getting-started",
    title: "Getting started",
    icon: "FileTextIcon",
    tooltip: "Learn the first steps to use Nocta UI",
    defaultOpen: true,
    children: [
      {
        id: "installation",
        title: "Installation",
        icon: "FileTextIcon",
        tooltip: "Install dependencies in a few commands",
      },
      {
        id: "project-setup",
        title: "Project setup",
        icon: "LayersIcon",
        tooltip: "Configure a new workspace layout",
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: "components",
    title: "Components",
    icon: "Component1Icon",
    tooltip: "Browse reusable UI building blocks",
    children: [
      {
        id: "layout-primitives",
        title: "Layout primitives",
        icon: "Component1Icon",
        tooltip: "Arrange pages with foundational sections",
      },
      {
        id: "data-display",
        title: "Data display",
        icon: "Component1Icon",
        tooltip: "Visualize stats and metrics clearly",
      },
      {
        id: "overlays",
        title: "Overlays & dialogs",
        icon: "Component1Icon",
        tooltip: "Work with modals, sheets, and popovers",
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: "accessibility",
    title: "Accessibility",
    icon: "QuestionMarkCircledIcon",
    tooltip: "Follow inclusive design best practices",
  },
  {
    id: "api-reference",
    title: "API reference",
    icon: "GearIcon",
    tooltip: "Review props and available configuration",
  },
];

const sidebarCommandItems: CommandKItem[] = [
  {
    label: "Introduction",
    group: "Documentation",
    description: "Overview of Nocta UI",
    icon: <RadixIcons.HomeIcon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },
  {
    label: "Getting started",
    group: "Documentation",
    description: "Installation & project setup",
    icon: <RadixIcons.FileTextIcon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },
  {
    label: "Components",
    group: "Documentation",
    description: "Browse component primitives",
    icon: <RadixIcons.Component1Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },
  {
    label: "API reference",
    group: "Documentation",
    description: "Props & configuration",
    icon: <RadixIcons.GearIcon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },

  {
    label: "Open repository",
    group: "Project",
    description: "View Nocta UI on GitHub",
    icon: <RadixIcons.GitHubLogoIcon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },
  {
    label: "View release notes",
    group: "Project",
    description: "See what’s new in this version",
    icon: <RadixIcons.UpdateIcon aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />,
  },
];

export function SidebarWorkspaceDemo() {
  const [activeItem, setActiveItem] = React.useState("introduction");
  const [openSections, setOpenSections] = React.useState<
    Record<string, boolean>
  >(() =>
    workspaceNavigation.reduce<Record<string, boolean>>((acc, item) => {
      if (item.defaultOpen) {
        acc[item.id] = true;
      }
      return acc;
    }, {}),
  );

  const handleSectionOpenChange = React.useCallback(
    (sectionId: string, nextOpen: boolean) => {
      setOpenSections((previous) => ({ ...previous, [sectionId]: nextOpen }));
    },
    [],
  );

  const isItemActive = React.useCallback(
    (item: (typeof workspaceNavigation)[number]) => {
      if (activeItem === item.id) {
        return true;
      }
      if (!item.children) {
        return false;
      }
      return item.children.some((child) => child.id === activeItem);
    },
    [activeItem],
  );

  return (
    <div className="w-full overflow-hidden sidebar">
      <SidebarProvider className="relative flex">
        <Sidebar>
          <SidebarHeader>
            <div className="flex items-center justify-start gap-1.5">
              <svg
                aria-hidden="true"
                width="22"
                height="22"
                viewBox="0 0 24 24"
                fill="none"
                xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
              >
                <path
                  fillRule="evenodd"
                  clipRule="evenodd"
                  d="M12 0C13.0265 0 14.0227 0.129607 14.9736 0.37207L19 9V2.25586C22.0271 4.43433 24 7.98574 24 12C24 18.6274 18.6274 24 12 24C10.9731 24 9.97671 23.8696 9.02539 23.627L5 15V21.7432C1.97313 19.5647 0 16.0141 0 12C0 5.37258 5.37258 0 12 0ZM12 5C8.13401 5 5 8.13401 5 12C5 15.866 8.13401 19 12 19C15.866 19 19 15.866 19 12C19 8.13401 15.866 5 12 5Z"
                  fill="currentColor"
                />
              </svg>
              <p className="text-base font-medium text-foreground">Nocta UI</p>
            </div>
            <SidebarInput
              items={sidebarCommandItems}
              placeholder="Search docs..."
            />
          </SidebarHeader>

          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarGroup>
              <div className="relative">
                <SidebarGroupLabel>Documentation</SidebarGroupLabel>
                <SidebarGroupAction aria-label="Add section">
                  <RadixIcons.PlusIcon className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />
                </SidebarGroupAction>
              </div>

              <SidebarGroupContent>
                <SidebarMenu>
                  {workspaceNavigation.map((item) => {
                    const hasChildren = Boolean(item.children?.length);
                    const collapsibleProps = hasChildren
                      ? {
                          open: Boolean(openSections[item.id]),
                          onOpenChange: (open: boolean) =>
                            handleSectionOpenChange(item.id, open),
                        }
                      : null;

                    const Icon = RadixIcons[item.icon];

                    return (
                      <SidebarMenuItem
                        key={item.id}
                        collapsible={hasChildren}
                        {...(collapsibleProps ?? {})}
                      >
                        <SidebarMenuButton
                          isActive={isItemActive(item)}
                          onClick={() => {
                            if (!hasChildren) {
                              setActiveItem(item.id);
                            }
                          }}
                          tooltip={item.tooltip}
                        >
                          <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
                            <Icon className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />
                            <span>{item.title}</span>
                          </span>
                        </SidebarMenuButton>

                        {hasChildren ? (
                          <SidebarMenuSub>
                            {item.children?.map((child) => {
                              const ChildIcon = RadixIcons[child.icon];

                              return (
                                <SidebarMenuSubItem key={child.id}>
                                  <SidebarMenuSubButton
                                    isActive={activeItem === child.id}
                                    onClick={() => setActiveItem(child.id)}
                                    tooltip={child.tooltip}
                                  >
                                    <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
                                      <ChildIcon
                                        className="size-4"
                                        aria-hidden="true"
                                      />
                                      <span>{child.title}</span>
                                    </span>
                                  </SidebarMenuSubButton>
                                </SidebarMenuSubItem>
                              );
                            })}
                          </SidebarMenuSub>
                        ) : null}
                      </SidebarMenuItem>
                    );
                  })}
                </SidebarMenu>
              </SidebarGroupContent>
            </SidebarGroup>

            <SidebarSeparator />
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Project</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarGroupContent>
                <SidebarMenu>
                  <SidebarMenuItem>
                    <SidebarMenuButton
                      isActive={activeItem === "repository"}
                      onClick={() => setActiveItem("repository")}
                      tooltip="View the GitHub project workspace"
                    >
                      <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
                        <RadixIcons.GitHubLogoIcon
                          className="size-4"
                          aria-hidden="true"
                        />
                        <span>Repository</span>
                      </span>
                    </SidebarMenuButton>
                  </SidebarMenuItem>
                </SidebarMenu>
              </SidebarGroupContent>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </SidebarContent>

          <SidebarFooter>
            <Button size="sm" className="w-full">
              View release notes
            </Button>
          </SidebarFooter>
        </Sidebar>

        <SidebarTrigger />

        <SidebarInset className="bg-background rounded-md grid grid-cols-3 grid-rows-3 gap-2 p-2 h-160">
          <div className="row-span-1 col-span-3 grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 w-full">
            <div className="h-full bg-card rounded-md" />
            <div className="h-full bg-card rounded-md" />
            <div className="h-full bg-card rounded-md" />
          </div>
          <div className="col-span-3 row-span-2 bg-card rounded-md" />
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## API Reference

### Providers and hooks

#### SidebarProvider

    children: {
      description: 'Sidebar layout, typically `<Sidebar>` plus `<SidebarInset>`. ',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    side: {
      description: 'Edge of the viewport the sidebar is anchored to.',

title: Skeleton
description: Loading skeleton component with variants, shapes, and animations for creating content placeholders during loading states

  BasicSkeletonDemo,
  ShimmerSkeletonDemo,
  WaveSkeletonDemo,
  SkeletonSizesDemo,

  TextLinesDemo,
  CustomSizeDemo,
  CardSkeletonDemo,

## Installation

Install the Skeleton component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add skeleton
```
Import the component:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton';
```

## Examples

### Default Skeleton

    <BasicSkeletonDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Default Skeleton"
    <Skeleton />
    ```

    <ShimmerSkeletonDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Shimmer Animation"
    <Skeleton variant="shimmer" />
    ```

### Sizes

    <SkeletonSizesDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Skeleton Sizes"
    <Skeleton size="sm" />
    <Skeleton size="md" />
    <Skeleton size="lg" />
    ```

### Shapes

    <ShapesDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Skeleton Shapes"
    {/* Rectangle */}
    <Skeleton shape="rectangle" width="12rem" height="3rem" />

    {/* Circle */}
    <Skeleton shape="circle" size="lg" />

    {/* Text (Single Line) */}
    <Skeleton shape="text" width="10rem" />

    {/* Text (Multiple Lines) */}
    <Skeleton shape="text" lines={3} />
    ```

### Text Lines

    <TextLinesDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Text Lines"
    <Skeleton shape="text" lines={2} />
    <Skeleton shape="text" lines={4} />
    <Skeleton shape="text" lines={6} />
    ```

### Custom Dimensions

    <CustomSizeDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Custom Dimensions"
    <Skeleton width="200px" height="60px" />

    <Skeleton shape="circle" width="80px" height="80px" />

    <Skeleton shape="text" width="150px" height="20px" />
    ```

## Api Reference

    variant: {
      description: 'Animation variant',
      type: '"default" | "shimmer"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Predefined size',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',
    shape: {
      description: 'Shape of the skeleton',
      type: '"rectangle" | "circle" | "text"',
      default: '"rectangle"',
    width: {
      description: 'Custom width',
      type: 'string | number',
    height: {
      description: 'Custom height',
      type: 'string | number',
    lines: {
      description: 'Number of text lines (only for text shape)',
      type: 'number',
      default: '1',
      description: 'Additional CSS classes',
      default: '""',

# table.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/table.mdx

title: Table
description: Fully accessible data table powered by TanStack Table and Ariakit composites.

import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";

  BasicTableDemo,
  SelectableTableDemo,
  CompactTableDemo

## Installation

    Install the Table component using the nocta-ui CLI:

    ```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
    npx @nocta-ui/cli add table
    ```
    Then import the component and supporting types:

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
    import { Table, type ColumnDef } from '@/components/ui/table';
    ```

## Examples

### Default Table

<DocsTabs justify="start"  defaultValue="preview">
    <BasicTableDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Table"
    interface Invoice {
      invoice: string;
      customer: string;
      status: 'paid' | 'processing' | 'overdue';
      issuedOn: Date;
      amount: number;
    }

    const currency = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
      style: 'currency',
      currency: 'USD',
      minimumFractionDigits: 0,
    });

    const columns: ColumnDef<Invoice>[] = [
      {
        accessorKey: 'invoice',
        header: 'Invoice',
        cell: ({ row }) => (
          <span className="font-medium">{row.getValue('invoice')}</span>
        ),
        meta: { width: '140px' },
      },
      {
        accessorKey: 'customer',
        header: 'Customer',
      },
      {
        accessorKey: 'issuedOn',
        header: 'Issued',
        cell: ({ getValue }) => {
          const date = getValue<Date>();
          return date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
            month: 'short',
            day: 'numeric',
            year: 'numeric',
          });
        },
        meta: { align: 'right', width: '160px' },
      },
      {
        accessorKey: 'amount',
        header: 'Amount',
        cell: ({ getValue }) => (
          <span className="font-medium">
            {currency.format(getValue<number>())}
          </span>
        ),
        meta: { align: 'right', width: '140px' },
      },
    ];

    const data: Invoice[] = [
      {
        invoice: 'INV-2041',
        customer: 'Lumen Studio',
        status: 'paid',
        issuedOn: new Date('2024-02-14'),
        amount: 2450,
      },
      // ...
    ];

    <Table<Invoice>
      columns={invoiceColumns}
      data={invoiceData}
      getRowId={(invoice) => invoice.invoice}
      density="comfortable"
	/>
    ```

### Row Selection

<DocsTabs justify="start" defaultValue="preview">
    <SelectableTableDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Row Selection"
    // columns and data defined as in the previous example
    const [selectedRows, setSelectedRows] = React.useState<Row<Invoice>[]>([]);

    <Table
      columns={invoiceColumns}
      data={invoiceData}
      getRowId={(invoice) => invoice.invoice}
      enableRowSelection
      onSelectedRowsChange={setSelectedRows}
      emptyState="No invoices yet"
    />

    ```

### Compact Density

<DocsTabs justify="start" defaultValue="preview">
    <CompactTableDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Compact Table"
    // Reuse your existing column and data definitions
    const teamColumns: ColumnDef<TeamMember>[] = [...];
    const teamMembers: TeamMember[] = [...];

    <Table
      columns={teamColumns}
      data={teamMembers}
      getRowId={(member) => member.name}
      density="compact"
    />
    ```

## API Reference

    columns: {
      description: 'Column definitions that describe the table structure.',
      type: 'ColumnDef<TData, unknown>[]',
    data: {
      description: 'Data records to render with the provided columns.',
      type: 'TData[]',
    density: {
      description: 'Controls overall padding and typography density.',
      type: '"comfortable" | "compact"',
      default: '"comfortable"',
    enableSorting: {
      description: "Toggles TanStack Table's sorting features.",
      default: 'true',
    enableRowSelection: {
      description: 'Adds a selection column with Ariakit-powered checkboxes.',
      default: 'false',
    activeRowId: {
      description: 'Marks a row as active for focus and highlighting.',
    onActiveRowChange: {
      description: 'Callback when the active row changes.',
      type: '(rowId: string | undefined) => void',
    onRowClick: {
      description: 'Fired when a table row is clicked.',
      type: '(row: Row<TData>) => void',
    initialSorting: {
      description: 'Default sorting state when uncontrolled.',
      type: 'SortingState',
      default: '[]',
    sortingState: {
      description: 'Controlled sorting state.',
      type: 'SortingState',
    onSortingChange: {
      description: 'Handler used with controlled sorting.',
      type: '(sorting: SortingState) => void',
    rowSelectionState: {
      description: 'Controlled selection state keyed by row id.',
      type: 'RowSelectionState',
    onRowSelectionChange: {
      description: 'Handler used with controlled selection.',
      type: '(state: RowSelectionState) => void',
    onSelectedRowsChange: {
      description: 'Emits the currently selected rows array.',
      type: '(rows: Row<TData>[]) => void',
    emptyState: {
      description: 'Custom UI shown when there are no rows.',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',
    getRowId: {
      description: 'Supplies custom logic for deriving stable row ids.',
      type: '(originalRow: TData, index: number, parent?: Row<TData>) => string',
      description: 'Additional Tailwind classes merged with the component styles.',
      default: '""',

# tabs.mdx

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Vertical Tabs"
              </CardDescription>
            </CardHeader>
            <CardContent>
              <p>General settings content.</p>
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        </TabsContent>
        {/* Other TabsContent components */}
      </div>
    </Tabs>
    ```

    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Disabled Tabs"
    </Tabs>
    ```

      description: 'Callback when tab changes',

    orientation: {
      description: 'Tabs orientation',
      type: '"horizontal" | "vertical"',
      default: '"horizontal"',
    variant: {
      description: 'Visual variant',
      type: '"default" | "pills" | "underline"',
      default: '"default"',
    size: {
      description: 'Size variant',
      type: '"sm" | "md" | "lg"',
      default: '"md"',

      default: '""',

      description: 'Disable all tabs',

      description: 'Trigger content',
      type: 'React.ReactNode',

      description: 'Disable this tab',
      default: 'false',

      default: '""',

# tanstack.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/tanstack.mdx

title: Tanstack Start Installation
description: Step-by-step guide to install and configure Nocta UI with Tanstack Start

## Create Tanstack Start Project

First, create a new Tanstack Start project:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npm create @tanstack/start@latest my-app --tailwind
cd my-app
```

## Install Nocta UI

Initialize Nocta UI in your project. This will automatically install all required dependencies:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli init
```

## Add Components

Now you can add specific components that you need:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add button
npx @nocta-ui/cli add card
npx @nocta-ui/cli add badge
```

## Usage

Now you can import and use Nocta UI components in your Tanstack Start application:

```tsx lineNumbers title="src/app/page.tsx"
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <div className="p-8">
      <Card className="max-w-md">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Welcome to Nocta UI</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <div className="space-y-4">
            <Button variant="default">
              Get Started
            </Button>
            <Badge variant="secondary">
              Next.js Ready
            </Badge>
          </div>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

You're all set! Use the Nocta UI CLI to pull components straight into your Tanstack Start application whenever you need them.

---

# toast.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/toast.mdx

title: Toast
description: Sonner-inspired toast notification system with CSS Transitions, smart stacking, and accessibility features

  BasicToastDemo,
  ToastVariantsDemo,
  ToastWithActionsDemo,
  StackedToastsDemo,
  PersistentToastDemo,
  CustomDurationDemo,
  DismissAllDemo,
  ToastPositionsDemo
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab"

## Installation

Install the Toast component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add toast
```
Import the components you need:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import { toast, Toaster } from '@/components/ui/toast';
```
Add the Toaster component to your app to enable toast notifications:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Toaster Setup"
import { Toaster } from '@/components/ui/toast';

function App() {
  return (
    <>
      <YourApp />
      <Toaster />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Default Toast

    <BasicToastDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Simple Toast"

    const showToast = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Success!',
        description: 'Your changes have been saved.',
      });
    };

    <Button onClick={showToast}>
      Show Toast
    </Button>
    ```

### Variants

    <ToastVariantsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Toast Variants"
    const showDefault = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Information',
        description: 'This is a default toast notification.',
      });
    };

    const showSuccess = () => {
      toast.success({
        title: 'Success!',
        description: 'Your operation completed successfully.',
      });
    };

    const showWarning = () => {
      toast.warning({
        title: 'Warning',
        description: 'Please check your input before continuing.',
      });
    };

    const showError = () => {
      toast.error({
        title: 'Error',
        description: 'Something went wrong. Please try again.',
      });
    };
    ```

### Positions

    <ToastPositionsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Toast Positions"
    const positions = [
      'top-left',
      'top-center',
      'top-right',
      'bottom-left',
      'bottom-center',
      'bottom-right'
    ];

    const showTopRight = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Top Right Toast',
        description: 'This toast appears in the top-right corner.',
        position: 'top-right',
      });
    };

    const showBottomLeft = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Bottom Left Toast',
        description: 'This toast appears in the bottom-left corner.',
        position: 'bottom-left',
        variant: 'success',
      });
    };
    ```

### Toast with Actions

    <ToastWithActionsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Toast with Actions"
    const showToast = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Update Available',
        description: 'A new version of the app is ready to install.',
        action: {
          label: 'Update',
          onClick: () => console.log('Update clicked!')
        }
      });
    };
    ```

### Stacked Toasts

    <StackedToastsDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Stacked Toasts"
    const showMultiple = () => {
      toast({ title: 'First Toast', description: 'This is the first notification.' });

      setTimeout(() => {
        toast.success({
          title: 'Second Toast',
          description: 'This is the second notification.',
        });
      }, 500);

      setTimeout(() => {
        toast.warning({
          title: 'Third Toast',
          description: 'This is the third notification.',
        });
      }, 1000);

      setTimeout(() => {
        toast.error({
          title: 'Fourth Toast',
          description: 'This will push the first one out!',
        });
      }, 1500);
    };
    ```

### Persistent Toast

    <PersistentToastDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Persistent Toast"
    const showToast = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Important Notice',
        description: 'This toast will remain visible until manually closed.',
        duration: 0,
      });
    };
    ```

### Custom Duration

    <CustomDurationDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Custom Toast Duration"
    const showToast = () => {
      toast({
        title: 'Quick Toast',
        description: 'This toast will close in 2 seconds.',
        duration: 2000,
      });
    };
    ```

### Dismiss All

    <DismissAllDemo />
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Dismiss All Toasts"
    const showMultiple = () => {
      toast({ title: 'Toast 1', description: 'First notification' });
      toast.success({ title: 'Toast 2', description: 'Second notification' });
      toast.warning({ title: 'Toast 3', description: 'Third notification' });
    };

    const handleDismissAll = () => {
      toast.dismissAll();
    };
    ```

### Default String Usage

```tsx lineNumbers title="Simple String Toasts"
toast('Simple message');
toast.success('Operation successful!');
toast.warning('Please be careful');
toast.error('Something went wrong');
```

## Api Reference

      description: 'Toast title',
    description: {
      description: 'Toast description',
    variant: {
      description: 'Toast style variant',
      type: '"default" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive"',
      default: '"default"',
      description: 'Custom CSS classes for styling',
    position: {
      description: 'Toast position on screen',
      type: '"top-left" | "top-center" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-center" | "bottom-right"',
      default: '"bottom-center"',
    duration: {
      description: 'Auto-close duration in ms (0 = persistent)',
      type: 'number',
      default: '5000',
    action: {
      description: 'Action button configuration',
      type: '{ label: string; onClick: () => void }',
    shouldClose: {
      description: 'Flag for programmatic closing with animation',
      default: 'false',

# toggle-group.mdx

Source: https://github.com/nocta-ui/nocta-ui/blob/main/apps/web/content/docs/toggle-group.mdx

title: Toggle Group
description: Grouped toggle buttons for single or multiple selection states with shared styling and keyboard support.

  BasicToggleGroupDemo,
  MultipleToggleGroupDemo,
  ToggleGroupSizesDemo,
  ToggleGroupWithIconsDemo
import { DocsTabs, DocsTab } from "@/components/docs-tab";

## Installation

Install the Toggle Group component using the nocta-ui CLI:

```bash lineNumbers title="Terminal"
npx @nocta-ui/cli add toggle-group
```

Import the components:

```tsx lineNumbers title="Import"
import {
  ToggleGroup,
  ToggleGroupItem
} from '@/components/ui/toggle-group';
```

## Examples

### Default Toggle Group

    <div className="my-6">
      <BasicToggleGroupDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Basic Toggle Group"
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>(['daily']);

    <ToggleGroup single value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="daily">Daily</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="weekly">Weekly</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="monthly">Monthly</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    ```

### Multiple Selection

    <div className="my-6">
      <MultipleToggleGroupDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Multiple Toggle Group"
    const [channels, setChannels] = useState<string[]>(['email']);

    <ToggleGroup value={channels} onValueChange={setChannels}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="email">Email</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="sms">SMS</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="push">Push</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    ```

### Sizes

    <div className="my-6">
      <ToggleGroupSizesDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Toggle Group Sizes"
    const [values, setValues] = useState({ sm: ['left'], md: ['center'], lg: ['right'] });

    <ToggleGroup single size="sm" value={values.sm} onValueChange={(next) => setValues(prev => ({ ...prev, sm: next }))}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    <ToggleGroup single size="md" value={values.md} onValueChange={(next) => setValues(prev => ({ ...prev, md: next }))}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    <ToggleGroup single size="lg" value={values.lg} onValueChange={(next) => setValues(prev => ({ ...prev, lg: next }))}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    ```

### Icon Toolbar

    <div className="my-6">
      <ToggleGroupWithIconsDemo />
    </div>
    ```tsx lineNumbers title="Icon Toggle Group"
    <ToggleGroup value={formats} onValueChange={setFormats} size="sm">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
        <FontBoldIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
        <FontItalicIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
        <UnderlineIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
    ```

## API Reference

### ToggleGroup

    single: {
      description: 'Determines whether only one item can be selected at a time.',
      default: 'false',
    value: {
      description: 'Controlled selected values.',
      type: 'string[]',
    defaultValue: {
      description: 'Initial selection for uncontrolled usage.',
      type: 'string[]',
      default: '[]',
    onValueChange: {
      description: 'Callback when the selection changes.',
      type: '(value: string[]) => void',
    variant: {
      description: 'Outer container style.',
